The "Baozhong Tea Festival" is a premier annual campus-wide event at National Chengchi University (NCCU), where departments from across the university come together to showcase the creativity and vitality of NCCU students through interactive booths, stage performances, and cultural exhibitions. Named after the famous local "Muzha Baozhong Tea" of the Wenshan District where the campus resides, the festival symbolizes the university’s deep humanistic roots and strong connection to the local community.
During the festival, each department sets up distinctive exhibition booths to introduce their academic features, curriculum design, and learning achievements, while hosting interactive games and cultural hands-on experiences. Concurrently, the main stage in front of the historic Siwei Hall features a vibrant lineup of live performances, including singing, dancing, drama, and creative talents.
The Department of Japanese Studies actively participates in this grand festival every year. In addition to delivering dynamic stage performances, our students design creative booths to introduce the department's academic highlights and cultural activities, beautifully conveying our core philosophy: "Learning Japanese is not just about mastering a language, but fully experiencing a rich culture."

Led by Professor Yuka Aoi, a delegation including two student teachers from Notre Dame Seishin University visited National Chengchi University (NCCU) for a three-day teaching practicum, experiencing Taiwan's unique cultural and educational landscape.
As aspiring Japanese language educators, the visiting students specifically chose this overseas practicum to broaden their teaching portfolios. During their time at the NCCU Department of Japanese, they observed core classes and engaged in multiple interactive sessions with our students to gain insight into how foreign languages are taught here. Throughout these exchanges, NCCU students demonstrated exceptional Japanese proficiency, communicating effortlessly and maintaining a smooth, barrier-free dialogue.
To maximize the value of this practicum, our department curated a multi-layered experience. Beyond passive classroom observations, the trainees actively participated in class dynamics and teaching simulations, blending pedagogical practice with genuine cultural exchange. This face-to-face initiative beautifully exemplified "Internationalization at Home"—allowing Taiwanese students to expand their global horizons and sharpen their practical language skills through peer-to-peer interaction without ever having to leave the country.

text:

Our department was deeply honored to welcome faculty and students from Hokusei Gakuen University, who traveled all the way from Hokkaido to join us for a memorable cross-cultural exchange. This event provided a wonderful platform for students from both universities to interact face-to-face and deepen their mutual understanding.
The exchange was conducted in small groups to cultivate a relaxed and welcoming atmosphere. The discussion topics were incredibly diverse: while some groups shared details about their respective campus lives, others dove into complex social and political issues. A few groups even took a casual stroll around our campus while chatting, naturally closing the distance between them through spontaneous interaction.
Although the time together was brief, the enthusiasm in the room was palpable, with many participants wishing they had more time to continue their conversations. The event concluded with a cheerful group photo, marking the friendly bonds built in a short time. We extend our heartfelt gratitude to the teachers and students of Hokusei Gakuen University for visiting NCCU, and we look forward to future opportunities to further deepen our exchange and partnership.

Do you think sushi is merely a combination of rice and raw fish? Did you know that Edomae Sushi, the predecessor of modern Nigiri sushi, is actually a flavorful universe steeped in aesthetics and philosophy?
This captivating lecture features Mr. Nai-Hao Li (also known as Master Bianshen), the acclaimed food critic and author of A Century of Washoku. He will guide the audience on a cultural journey tracing the evolution of sushi from Edo-period street carts to contemporary high-end dining. Moving beyond simple culinary history, this talk will deconstruct every step of sushi-making through a metaphysical lens, exploring the deep relationships between ingredients, craftsmanship, and the final culinary creation.
Whether you are a dedicated foodie, a Japanese cuisine enthusiast, or a student of food culture studies, you are warmly invited to join this philosophical and sensory intellectual journey!

This year, the Department of Japanese Studies proudly participated in the 59th NCCU Culture Cup Choral Competition, performing the iconic Japanese graduation song, "Letters: Greetings to a 15-Year-Old You" (手紙 〜拝啓 十五の君へ〜). The piece beautifully conveys a message of resilience—that even when feeling lost during one's academic journey, the future remains bright and worth embracing—perfectly echoing the youthful voices of our students.
With a lineup larger and more enthusiastic than ever, students dedicated every Wednesday evening to rigorous rehearsals, pouring their hearts into crafting the most moving harmonies. Ultimately, their collective dedication culminated in a breathtaking performance on the Culture Cup stage, bringing this journey of teamwork and shared passion to a brilliant and memorable close.

Through this information session, students not only gained deep insights into the corporate core values of Lion Travel but also developed a more comprehensive understanding of the diverse roles within the tourism industry.
Professor Kuo-Ching Wang specially introduced the relevant details of the global bootcamp and overseas internship programs, both of which are rich in content and represent rare, invaluable learning opportunities for students. Although participating in these internships will bring challenges and high-pressure situations, the professional experience accumulated and the professional networks built through teamwork throughout the process will undoubtedly become essential assets for the students' future careers.

To foster meaningful exchanges between our graduated alumni and current faculty and students, our department is proudly hosting the Alumni Homecoming Forum.
Through a structured yet relaxed panel discussion, invited alumni will share their postgraduate academic journeys and diverse career experiences. This event offers current students valuable insights into their future career paths while strengthening professional networks and personal bonds within the departmental community.

"NCCU Japanese Night" is a grand annual signature event hosted by the Department of Japanese Studies at National Chengchi University. Entrusted entirely to the creativity of our students, the night is independently planned, organized, and performed to showcase their achievements in learning the Japanese language and embracing its culture.
Beyond a cultural showcase, this vibrant evening serves as a vital platform for strengthening departmental bonds and fostering meaningful exchanges with the wider community.

Our department was honored to host Professor Toshihiro Ichida and his student delegation from the School of Commerce, Waseda University. A wonderful academic exchange session was held during their visit, creating invaluable networking and learning opportunities for students from both universities.

Hello! Ready to build an extraordinary life experience?
Welcome to the "Hubble Star Project," a global talent incubation program jointly created by Lion Travel Group and National Taiwan Normal University (NTNU). Designed to inject new blood into the tourism industry, this program is your gateway to becoming a well-rounded, international professional.
Program Highlights:
Bootcamp Training: Immersive learning at Lion Travel Headquarters.
Overseas Internships: Gain firsthand global experience at branch offices worldwide. ✈️
Management Trainee: Secure a fast-track contract to kickstart and shine in your career!
Who We Are Looking For:
If you are passionate about tourism, leisure, hospitality, or management, and are driven by endless enthusiasm—join us today! Let’s unlock your potential and transform you into the brightest star. ★

text:

[:::](http:japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageAlbum/Detail?fid=10311&id=3241#accesskey-c)

For this academic event, our department was deeply honored to invite Professor Tomomi Suzuki from the Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (TUFS) to deliver a guest lecture via videoconferencing.
Professor Suzuki, whose long-term research focuses on the dictionary-consulting behaviors of second language learners, analyzed the common difficulties learners face and the limitations of current online dictionaries from a learner-centric perspective. During the webinar, she also introduced an innovative Japanese example sentence database she developed, shedding light on the critical characteristics that constitute an ideal example sentence for language learners.

title: Detail?fid=10311&id=3407
text:
[:::](http:japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageAlbum/Detail?fid=10311&id=3407#accesskey-l)

[:::](http:japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageAlbum/Detail?fid=10311&id=3407#accesskey-c)

In this lecture, Professor Sekiguchi addressed the theme of "Making Japanese Language Classes Fun and Easy to Understand Through ICT Integration," exploring how Information and Communications Technology (ICT) can enhance engagement and comprehension in language pedagogy.
During the session, the speaker demonstrated the practical application of the Wordwall platform, guiding participants through hands-on classroom activities. Through gamified design, conventional and repetitive drills are transformed into learning activities that are both enjoyable and challenging. Furthermore, Wordwall offers the flexibility to adapt to various learning objectives; by synchronously integrating "semantics, text, and audio," it effectively aids learners in memory retention.
This lecture beautifully showcased the diverse possibilities of ICT in language acquisition, illustrating how digital tools can cultivate a more dynamic classroom atmosphere while making Japanese learning interactive and accessible.

For this academic event, our department was honored to invite Professor Kei Ishiguro from the National Institute for Japanese Language and Linguistics (NINJAL) to deliver a guest lecture. Professor Ishiguro introduced the characteristics of Japanese youth slang from two dimensions: language evolution and the nuanced differences resulting from various vocabulary choices.
The lecture featured a wealth of contemporary examples. Notably, Professor Ishiguro's daughter, Ms. Ai Ishiguro, who is currently a university student, also attended the event to share firsthand insights into the precise meanings and usage of modern youth terms. Furthermore, from the perspective of language change, the professor systematically classified youth slang into categories such as "temporary fads" and "regional slang."
During the Q&A session, students actively engaged with the speaker, and everyone in attendance walked away with a wealth of knowledge from Professor Ishiguro's brilliant presentation.

In recent years, an increasing number of liberal arts students have successfully forged rewarding paths within the technology sector. Even without a traditional technical background, individuals with a strong passion for learning can thrive and excel. This corporate session introduces Garmin's tailored talent cultivation initiatives and career growth opportunities, illustrating how humanities and liberal arts majors can successfully transition into the tech industry.
Garmin provides comprehensive training frameworks and continuous learning mechanisms designed to help non-technical students gradually build essential skill sets and gain deep insights into tech operations and long-term career trajectories.
Through this briefing, students can explore a diverse array of professional roles within the tech ecosystem and discover the unique value that a liberal arts background brings to the industry—opening up inspiring new horizons for their future career mapping. We warmly welcome all students interested in technology or cross-disciplinary career development to join this event.

The 58th NCCU Culture Cup is a grand annual campus tradition hosted by National Chengchi University. Aimed at promoting cultural exchange among faculty, students, and the community, it showcases the diverse creativity and cultural literacy of NCCU students. Combining elements of art, culture, and entertainment, it has become one of the most iconic cultural events on campus.
In this year's competition, our department made a unique appearance wearing traditional Japanese Yukata and performed the classic Japanese choral piece, "Cosmos," which signifies the essence of the universe. Though small in size, our exquisite team delivered highly harmonious tones and touched the audience's hearts with rising melodies. The performance concluded with a curtain call in Japanese, fully demonstrating our deep affection for the culture we study.

Inspired by Natsume Soseki’s literary masterpiece Ten Nights of Dreams (夢十夜), this year's Japanese Night featured an innovative script that woven a deeply moving love story spanning over a century. Beyond the captivating theatrical drama, the showcase integrated live bands and dance troupes, displaying a diverse and mesmerizing stage charisma.
The student band delivered a breathtaking, high-caliber musical performance, while the dance crew crafted a stunning visual feast with high-energy choreography and dynamic lighting design, fully showcasing the students' immense talent and dedication.
Yet, a spectacular production relies not only on the performers in the spotlight but also on the tireless efforts of the entire backstage crew. From the chief and deputy coordinators, public relations, copywriting, video production, visual design, props, costumes, and makeup, to script translation and general administration—as well as the reception, stage management, lighting, and sound crews on the night of the event—every member's seamless collaboration was vital. It is this collective passion from both cast and crew that made this year's Japanese Night an unforgettable success, beautifully carrying forward the proudest tradition of the Department of Japanese.

This special lecture, organized in collaboration with Kobe University, offers a multi-faceted exploration designed to give students a comprehensive understanding of Japan. The presentation covers a rich array of topics, including contemporary Japanese culture, social structures, daily lifestyles, as well as practical pathways for future study abroad and career development.
Whether you are passionate about Japanese cultural studies or actively planning to pursue academic and professional opportunities in Japan, this session promises to provide highly practical insights, strategic advice, and valuable first-hand experiences to guide your future endeavors.

The JAL Presentation Contest is an annual competition hosted by Japan Airlines (JAL). It aims to provide a platform for university students to showcase their Japanese language proficiency while fostering cultural exchange between Taiwan and Japan.
Each year, students from our department proactively participate in this event, achieving outstanding results through their hard work and dedication. We hope their success inspires future students to challenge themselves and pursue their goals!

text:
[:::](http:japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageAlbum/Detail?fid=10311&id=3409#accesskey-l)

[:::](http:japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageAlbum/Detail?fid=10311&id=3409#accesskey-c)

Our department hosted a corporate information session featuring DISCO Corporation, a global leader in the semiconductor industry. The presentation covered the company’s history, core business operations, and future outlook, while highlighting its employee-friendly working environment and distinctive corporate culture, providing students with a deep understanding of this industry giant.
A special highlight of the event was the return of an esteemed department alumna now working at DISCO. She shared her firsthand professional journey, discussing the transition from campus to the corporate world, the challenges and rewards of her role, and the vital role of maintaining the right mindset during internships—offering highly inspiring takeaways for all attendees.

title: Detail?fid=10311&id=3556
text:
[:::](http:japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageAlbum/Detail?fid=10311&id=3556#accesskey-l)

[:::](http:japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageAlbum/Detail?fid=10311&id=3556#accesskey-c)

While we often perceive "Japanese" or "Korean" as fixed categories defined by nationality or lineage, history reveals that identity is a dynamic and evolving construct.
This special lecture features Professor Hosanna, who will guide the audience across national borders from the macro-perspective of comparative cultural studies. The presentation deconstructs how nations within the East Asian cultural sphere, specifically Japan and South Korea, have adapted to shifting historical eras to continuously redefine themselves and their concepts of citizenship and belonging.

During this event, students from Meio University were divided into four groups to deliver 10-minute Japanese presentations focusing on four core themes: Okinawa's history, culture, nature, and society, guiding NCCU students to explore Okinawa from various perspectives.
Following the presentations, a free discussion and networking session was held, giving students from both universities the opportunity to exchange views on the presentation topics and share their own cultural perspectives. This served as an excellent opportunity not only to practice Japanese listening and speaking skills but also to deepen understanding of Okinawa.

title: Detail?fid=10311&id=3781
text:
[:::](http:japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageAlbum/Detail?fid=10311&id=3781#accesskey-l)

[:::](http:japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageAlbum/Detail?fid=10311&id=3781#accesskey-c)

This special cultural exchange was seamlessly integrated into our department's "Japanese Conversation Drill (I)" course, providing students from both National Chengchi University and Yokohama City University (YCU) with a valuable opportunity to apply their language skills in a practical setting.
As many visiting students from YCU had previously studied Chinese, the peers from both universities engaged in lively dialogues by alternating between Chinese and Japanese. They shared various topics, including Taiwanese culture, personal hobbies, and daily student life. This tandem language interaction not only maximized the practical usage of their target languages but also greatly deepened their mutual understanding of each other's lifestyle and cultural background.
By fostering an authentic and natural communicative environment, this classroom exchange successfully enhanced our students' conversational proficiency, expanded their international horizons, and marked another positive milestone in deepening ties between Taiwanese and Japanese youth.

title: Detail?fid=10311&id=3792
text:
[:::](http:japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageAlbum/Detail?fid=10311&id=3792#accesskey-l)

[:::](http:japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageAlbum/Detail?fid=10311&id=3792#accesskey-c)

Our department was deeply honored to host Professor Michael Lucken from the Department of Japanese Studies at the French National Institute for Oriental Languages and Civilizations (INALCO) for an illuminating lecture titled "The Occupation as Postwar Intellectual History" (戦後思想史としての占領/occupation), guiding faculty and students through a profound exploration of pivotal issues in Japan's modern intellectual development.
Professor Lucken began his analysis by dissecting the subtle semantic differences between the Japanese term "Senryo" (占領) and the English word "Occupation," illustrating how the postwar rule of the Allied forces was perceived through contrasting lenses by Japan and the United States. He further examined the 1943 U.S. Military Field Manual FM 27-5 alongside various reform policies implemented during the GHQ era, demonstrating how American Pragmatism profoundly influenced and reshaped the landscape of postwar Japanese thought.
This lecture not only provided attendees with a critical re-evaluation of the historic GHQ era but also inspired deep reflection on the enduring impacts that this unique historical experience has left on contemporary Japanese society and philosophy.

On December 25, 2024, faculty and students from Putai High School visited National Chengchi University (NCCU) for an engaging campus tour and exchange. This visit allowed students to experience the university's academic environment and cultural atmosphere firsthand, offering valuable insights for their future higher education paths.
Professor Chi-Hao Kao represented our department to welcome the visitors and introduce our academic programs. We sincerely hope all the students will have the opportunity to join the NCCU family or successfully get into their dream universities!

title: Detail?fid=10311&id=3786
text:
[:::](http:japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageAlbum/Detail?fid=10311&id=3786#accesskey-l)

[:::](http:japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageAlbum/Detail?fid=10311&id=3786#accesskey-c)

To deepen mutual understanding and foster long-term friendships between the younger generations of Taiwan and Japan, the "35th Japan University Student Delegation to Taiwan"—jointly organized by Japan Airlines (JAL) and the Japan-Taiwan Youth Exchange Association—visited the Department of Japanese at National Chengchi University (NCCU) on March 5.
This year’s delegation brought together 10 outstanding Japanese students from prestigious institutions, including Waseda University, Tokyo International University, Nihon University, Utsunomiya University, Toyo University, Dokkyo University, Tokyo University of Industry, Kyoto Sangyo University, and Kansai Gaidai University. They engaged in deep cultural exchanges with 15 student representatives from our department.
During the visit, the delegation toured the Chi-Tao Building, which is beautifully nestled in the campus's lush natural surroundings. Through breakout group discussions and interactive activities, Taiwanese and Japanese students enjoyed rare face-to-face dialogues, sharing their campus lives and unique cultural experiences in a relaxed, friendly atmosphere that further solidified the bilateral ties.

text:
[:::](http:japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageAlbum/Detail?fid=10311&id=3552#accesskey-l)

[:::](http:japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageAlbum/Detail?fid=10311&id=3552#accesskey-c)

While our student exchange community traditionally hosts an annual Christmas party, the event was transformed into a Halloween celebration this year due to the university's transition to the new 16-week semester system.
On the day of the event, the venue was filled with a vibrant Halloween atmosphere as many participating students dressed up in creative costumes. Attendees enjoyed pizza while chatting casually and teaming up for classic party games inspired by popular Taiwanese variety shows. The lively gathering provided a fantastic opportunity for students to bond across different year groups, meet new international friends, and deepen their cross-cultural connections.

The annual Alumni Homecoming Day serves as a vital platform for our graduates to reconnect, share life updates, and exchange valuable career insights, while offering current students a precious opportunity to seek guidance and mentorship from their seniors. By fostering dynamic interactions between alumni and undergraduates, this gathering aims to strengthen intergenerational bonds, pass down the core values of our department, and inspire new possibilities for future development.
The event featured a rich lineup of activities, including insightful alumni career panels, engaging roundtable discussions, and heartwarming moments of catching up, allowing all participants to rediscover the warmth, solidarity, and enduring community spirit of their alma mater in a relaxed and joyful atmosphere.

The Freshman Orientation Camp is designed to help incoming students quickly acclimate to university life, build meaningful social connections, and familiarize themselves with campus resources and extracurricular opportunities.
The camp encourages students to explore, embrace new challenges, and actively participate in campus life. It emphasizes achieving a healthy balance between academic pursuits and personal well-being, placing equal weight on professional expertise and liberal arts education. Our ultimate goal is to nurture well-rounded individuals who possess both humanistic sensibilities and technological competencies, rooted in local engagement while embracing a global vision.

Japanese Language Teaching Workshop: How to Determine Student Grades and Assessments? — Real-World Experience Sharing from Japanese Language Educators
This workshop features experienced Japanese language teachers sharing their real-world case studies, insights, and strategic considerations regarding grading and assessment. The session aims to help current faculty members and students aspiring to pursue a career in Japanese language education gain a deeper understanding of how to design and apply effective grading rubrics.
Anyone passionate about Japanese language pedagogy is warmly invited to join the discussion and exchange ideas!

title: Detail?fid=10311&id=3790
text:
[:::](http:japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageAlbum/Detail?fid=10311&id=3790#accesskey-l)

[:::](http:japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageAlbum/Detail?fid=10311&id=3790#accesskey-c)

Centered on the theme of "Interactional Competence Revealed Through Conversation Analysis: A Focus on Japanese Conversations Involving Chinese Speakers," this lecture delves into the conversational characteristics and interactional strategies demonstrated by native Chinese speakers within Japanese communicative contexts.
Through the structural analysis of authentic conversation data, the session guides participants to understand how language users navigate dialogue, deploy interactional strategies, and manage various factors that influence communication outcomes. It further highlights both the competence and the pragmatic challenges faced by Japanese language learners during cross-linguistic interactions.
Bridging theoretical research with practical linguistic analysis, this lecture not only deepens the understanding of Japanese conversational proficiency but also offers fresh pedagogical perspectives on communicative skills. It is highly recommended for faculty and students interested in Japanese language education, applied linguistics, and intercultural communication.

This academic lecture explores the historical trajectory of social movements in Japan following World War II, including student activism and anti-war movements, and examines how these movements profoundly influenced the creation of literature, cinema, and fine arts.
Furthermore, the presentation offers a comparative analysis of the similarities and differences between social movements in Taiwan and Japan, prompting participants to reflect on the deeper societal significance underlying these cultural phenomena.

title: Detail?fid=10311&id=3168
text:
[:::](http:japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageAlbum/Detail?fid=10311&id=3168#accesskey-l)

[:::](http:japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageAlbum/Detail?fid=10311&id=3168#accesskey-c)

For this lecture, our department was pleased to invite Professor Toshiyuki Sadanobu from Kyoto University once again. Focusing on the theme of "Disfluency in Japanese Speech," the session explored what makes daily conversation sound natural.
Professor Sadanobu kicked off the lecture with an interactive survey, asking the audience to evaluate the naturalness of various voice recordings. He then thoroughly explained the critical nuances that made certain phrases sound authentic or awkward to native ears.
The lecture revealed that casual everyday conversations do not always need to flow perfectly like a news broadcast. In fact, appropriately incorporating fillers such as "eeto" (uh) or "un" (hmm) can make speech sound significantly more natural and native.

This information session provided students with a comprehensive overview of the upcoming overseas internship opportunities. The speakers delivered detailed explanations covering key aspects of the program, including unique project features, application procedures, and crucial prerequisites, giving attendees a well-rounded understanding of interning in Japan.
During the interactive Q&A session, speakers directly addressed the most frequently asked questions and student concerns. The atmosphere was highly engaging, with participants fully focused throughout the event. Through this briefing, students not only gained clarity on how global work experience impacts cross-cultural exchange and career mapping, but were also inspired to weigh the valuable rewards and unique challenges of participating in such programs.

"Youth in Action" is a municipal governance internship and action pilot program specially designed for young people to engage in public affairs. It aims to cultivate social awareness, deepen understanding of city government operations, and inspire innovative thinking and action.
Through attending this seminar, participants will gain deep insights into the policymaking process and receive valuable, firsthand experience in public affairs. This program serves not only as a learning platform but also as a catalyst inspiring the youth to contribute to the future development of our cities.

title: Detail?fid=10311&id=3555
text:
[:::](http:japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageAlbum/Detail?fid=10311&id=3555#accesskey-l)

[:::](http:japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageAlbum/Detail?fid=10311&id=3555#accesskey-c)

This full-day exchange event began in the morning with a special academic lecture titled "The Flow of Cross-Cultural Exchange in Contemporary Japanese Cinema," delivered by Professor Alec McAulay from Yokohama National University. The session explored various cross-cultural elements and interactive dynamics portrayed in modern Japanese films, followed by a collaborative workshop where Taiwanese and Japanese students co-created short screenplays and shared their work in groups to foster deep cross-cultural understanding.
During lunch, students from both universities engaged in casual, free-flowing conversations, gaining insights into each other's daily lives and cultural nuances.
The afternoon session kicked off with YNU students introducing Japan’s traditional seasonal food culture alongside an overview of their home institution, followed by a warm gift exchange. In return, our department students delivered presentations in English and Japanese showcasing Taiwan's rich culinary culture, sparking an enthusiastic Q&A session. The event concluded with reflection sharing and thoughtful dialogue regarding cultural observations. Overall, this exchange provided a valuable platform to enhance language proficiency, broaden global horizons, and build lasting bilateral friendships.

title: Detail?fid=10311&id=3405
text:
[:::](http:japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageAlbum/Detail?fid=10311&id=3405#accesskey-l)

[:::](http:japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageAlbum/Detail?fid=10311&id=3405#accesskey-c)

Faculty members from Kobe University in Japan visited our campus to host an admissions and exchange program information session. Through this event, students gained a deeper understanding of Kobe University’s academic curriculum and campus life, providing them with a clearer roadmap for future exchange opportunities or postgraduate studies in Japan.
During the presentation, the visiting professors highlighted Kobe University’s unique campus environment. Notably, due to its hilly and undulating terrain, navigating the campus provides students with an effortless daily workout, and there are even occasional opportunities to spot local wildlife on school grounds.
This session not only provided wealth of academic and practical information but also served as an inspiring starting point for students planning their study abroad journeys in Japan.

Our department's annual "Study Abroad and Exchange Programs Information Session" is designed to take you on a deep dive into a pivotal question: Why is it worth stepping outside the campus gates and heading to Japan—or even other dynamic regions across Asia?
This session will guide you on how to discover your own unique, resume-boosting milestones along NCCU's tailored pathway of "Japanese Language + Culture + International Outlook." Personal growth begins the very moment you step onto the global stage; join us to start mapping out your international journey!

To help students gain a deeper understanding of Japanese corporate operations and explore potential career opportunities, our department hosted the NITORI Corporate Information Session on May 5, 2025.
As a renowned Japanese retail giant, NITORI is dedicated to providing high-quality yet affordable home furnishings. In recent years, the company has been aggressively expanding its global footprint, establishing a strong and rapidly growing presence with numerous retail stores across Taiwan.

For [Course Search System](https://qrysub.nccu.edu.tw/)

List of Required Courses for the M.A. Program in the Department of Japanese Literature

Please refer to the attached file.

(For M.A. Students)

To ensure that students do not miss any necessary procedures, we have prepared the following guide.

Once you complete all the steps listed below, you will be eligible for graduation!

The full graduation regulations can be downloaded under “Downloads” → “Rules & Regulations”.

【Academic Research Ethics Education】

Starting from the 2016 academic year (105 AY), all M.A. students must complete and pass the Academic Research Ethics Education Course before the end of their first academic year. Students who fail to pass the course will not be allowed to apply for the degree examination.

How to take the course:

Students must complete a 4-hour online course and pass the assessment. If the test is not passed, the course must be retaken.

Course information can be found at: Office of Academic Affairs → Registration Section → Academic Research Ethics Education

【Graduation Procedures】For students enrolled before 2020 academic year (109 AY)

1.    Thesis Topic Presentation

o    Submit the “Thesis Topic Presentation Application Form” to the department office by the designated date. On the day of presentation, bring enough copies of the presentation materials for all attendees.

o    Recommended timing: After completing the thesis structure in the first year, present at the end of the semester. If not completed, present the following semester.

Required thesis structure

① Title & Subtitle

② Research Motivation

③ Methodology

④ Literature Review

⑤ Content

⑥ Table of Contents

⑦ References

(Presentation duration: approx. 20 minutes)

　　1. Mid-term Presentation

Submit the “Mid-term Thesis Presentation Application Form” (including names of committee members and presentation time) and presentation materials to the department office at least two weeks before the presentation.

After presenting, report your thesis title via the iNCCU system as required by the university.

Recommended timing: In the second year, when 50–70% of the thesis is completed, any time before the oral defense.

 

　　2. Thesis Oral Defense

Submit the “Application for Degree Examination” to the department office before the academic leave deadline of the semester in which the defense is scheduled. Late submissions will not be accepted.

Students who fail to apply and have not reached the maximum period of leave will be considered on leave. Those who have reached the limit will be dismissed.

Submit the draft thesis and notify the department of the defense schedule at least two weeks before the oral defense. The department will send out the committee invitation letters along with the thesis draft.

On the day of the defense, download and fill out the “Thesis Oral Examination Report” and the “Signature Page” in advance from the “Downloads” section.

Recommended timing: After completing 100% of the thesis in the 3rd or 4th year, schedule the defense by January 31 or July 31 of the intended graduation semester.

Starting August 1, 2019, degree exam applications must follow Article 3, Paragraph 2 of the NCCU Graduate Degree Examination Guidelines. This includes:

Thesis plagiarism check via the university system

Advisor’s signature

Departmental preliminary review and approval

Final submission to the Office of Academic Affairs for secondary review

Committee qualifications must comply with Articles 6 and 7 of the guidelines. Qualifications under Clauses 3 and 4 are determined by the relevant department or college committee.

Turnitin Account for Plagiarism Check:

Request an account from the department office

Activate the account via instructions sent to your NCCU email

Submit your thesis via the designated course page and click “Submit” for similarity check

 

【Graduation Procedures】For students enrolled from the 2020 academic year (109 AY) onward

1.Thesis Proposal Presentation

Students must submit and orally present their thesis proposal by the end of the first semester of their second year.

The proposal must include:

	(1) Thesis Title

	(2) Research Purpose and Motivation

	(3) Research Method

	(4) Scope of Research

	(5) Literature Review

	(6) References

The presentation must be reviewed and approved by 3 to 5 professors (assistant professor or above).

Submit the proposal to the department office at least two weeks prior for distribution to the reviewers.

If the proposal is not approved, students may apply for a second presentation. From the second attempt onward, all related costs are the student’s responsibility.

2.Thesis Oral Defense

After completing the thesis and receiving approval from the advisor, students may apply for the oral defense before the academic leave deadline.

Submit the signed application form (with plagiarism check and advisor’s approval) to the department office.

Note: Same procedures and regulations apply as noted in the section above (as of August 1, 2019).

Turnitin Account for Plagiarism Check:

Same steps as outlined in the earlier section.

 

3.Graduation and Departure Procedures

From August 1, 2015 (104 AY), students who pass the oral defense must complete thesis upload and departure procedures within one month of the start of the following semester (by September 1 or March 1).

Students who cannot finish in time may apply for delayed graduation (see Note 1).

Students who exceed the maximum period of study and fail to graduate will be dismissed.

Those who apply for delayed graduation and wish to adjust the graduation date must fill out the “Graduation Intent Adjustment Form”.

Note 1: Indicate the intention to delay graduation when submitting the “Application for Degree Examination.” Students delaying graduation must still register and pay tuition.

The Office of Registration prepares diplomas for students expected to graduate each semester. If students fail to graduate on time, a fee of NT$150 will be charged to reprint the diploma.

The actual date of diploma issuance may vary.

Thesis upload instructions are available on the “NCCU Electronic Thesis & Dissertation System” → “Upload Thesis”.

Two hardbound copies must be submitted to the library, and two to the department office.

Students are responsible for any consequences due to failure to comply with the above procedures.

Refer to the semester calendar for official deadlines and leave dates.

title: 國立政治大學日本語文學系碩士班研究生攻讀學位暨資格考試辦法(109前).pdf
text:
國立政治大學日本語文學系碩士班研究生攻讀學位暨資格考試辦法
經94年1月3日系務會議通過
經96年12月27日系務會議修訂
經98年3月5日系務會議修訂
經101年4月26日系務會議修訂
一、 本辦法依據〈國立政治大學研究生學位考試要點〉及相關規章訂定。
二、 本系碩士班研究生入學時，須於語言、文學、歷史三領域中，擇定一項為其研究專業，並
向系主任、相關領域教授及研究生導師諮商後，選擇修讀學系之課程科目，並於第二學年
第一學期選定論文指導教授。進入研究所就讀後，如欲更換研究專業，須經研究生導師與
系主任同意，始得變更。
三、 研究生須通過三次審查始得畢業，含論文撰寫計劃、論文期中發表及論文口試，其規定分
述如下：
１、 論文撰寫計劃：研究生應於第一學年結束前，於本系規定之時間統一發表論文撰寫計劃（包
含論文題目、研究方法、先行研究之整理），通過校內外三至五名助理教授級以上教師之審
查後，始得開始撰寫論文。未通過者，應於三個月內再次發表，以此類推。
２、 論文期中發表：研究生應於第二學年結束前向系辦提出論文期中發表之申請。若指導教授判
斷研究生未達論文期中發表之標準，得延後提出申請，唯原則上應於第三學年結束前完成發
表。
研究生提出申請後，經指導教授推薦及邀請校內外三至五名助理教授級以上之教師擔任口試
委員；並由系方安排於二至四週內舉行論文期中發表。論文期中發表得開放系上教師及研究
生旁聽，唯發表後，由委員將成績提交系辦。
論文期中發表成績以七十分為及格，一百分為滿分。成績不及格者，得申請重考，唯自第二
次發表起，因論文期中發表產生之所有費用，概由研究生自行負擔。
研究生通過論文期中發表後，經系主任、指導教授之核可，於本校規定期限內，向教務處完
成申報論文題目之手續。
３、 論文口試：研究生完成論文撰寫後，經指導教授同意，於當學期休學截止日前申請論文口
試。研究生提出申請後，由本系系方安排於二至四週內（學期結束日前）舉行論文口試。論
文口試依〈國立政治大學研究生學位考試要點〉相關規定辦理。
四、 本辦法經系務會議通過後施行，修正時亦同。

title: 國立政治大學日本語文學系碩士班研究生攻讀學位暨資格考試辦法(109.06.22).pdf
text:
國立政治大學日本語文學系碩士班研究生攻讀學位暨資格考試辦法
經94年1月3日系務會議通過
經96年12月27日系務會議修訂
經98年3月5日系務會議修訂
經101年4月26日系務會議修訂
經108年11月4日系務會議修訂
經109年4月13日系務會議修訂
經109年6月22日系務會議修訂
一、 本辦法依據〈國立政治大學研究生學位考試要點〉及相關規章訂定。
二、 研究領域暨指導教授選定辦法
1.本系碩士班研究生應於第一學年第二學期初，從語言、文學、歷史文化三領域中，擇定一
項為研究領域，並於本系公告之統一時間提出研究領域申請書。
2.本系碩士班研究生應於第二學年第一學期選定論文指導教授。
3.研究領域選定後，如欲更換研究領域，則須獲新舊指導教授同意後，繳交研究領域變更表
(使用系辦之申請書，須有新舊指導教授簽名)，並由新指導教授判斷是否承認之前所修學
分，經研究生導師與系主任同意，始得變更。
4.指導教授選定後，如欲變更指導教授，則須繳交指導教授變更表(使用學校既有之申請書即
可，須有新舊指導教授簽名)，並經研究生導師與系主任同意，始得變更。
三、 研究生畢業學分為二十八學分(含論文零學分)。
四、 研究生畢業之修業條件：
1.將本研究所之語言、文學、歷史文化三領域分為 AB 兩大學群，A 群為語言學群(含語言、
日語教育)，B 群為文化學群(含文學、歷史文化)。各學群之研究生，須於學位論文提交
前，修畢該學群之相關課程至少十四學分。
2.學位論文提交前，須於校內外學術研討會、研究生論文發表會(不含本系所之論文計劃書口
頭發表)或學術期刊發表至少一次。或參與以下學術活動至少四次(需提交參加證明)：
(1)校內外學術研討會、學術工作坊
(2)研究生論文發表會(不含本系所之論文計劃書口頭發表)
(3)學術性演講
五、 研究生須通過二次審查始得畢業，含論文計劃書及論文口試，其規定分述如下：
1. 論文計劃書：研究生應於第二學年第一學期結束前，於本系規定之時間統一提出論文計劃
書並進行口頭發表。
論文計劃書內容應包含下列各項：
(1)論文題目
(2)研究目的與動機
(3)研究方法
(4)研究範圍
(5)先行研究
(6)參考書目
2. 口頭發表須經校內外至少三名助理教授級以上教師（含指導教授）之審查通過後，始得開
始撰寫論文。口頭發表前一週須提交論文計劃書至審查委員或繳交至系辦，再由系辦轉交

給相關領域之審查委員。口頭發表未通過者，得申請重考，唯自第二次發表起，因論文計
劃書產生之所有費用，概由研究生自行負擔。
3. 論文口試：研究生完成論文撰寫後，經指導教授同意，於當學期休學截止日前申請論文口
試。研究生填具學位考試申請書，其論文經校內論文抄襲比對系統比對、送請指導教授簽
名同意、並經系主任簽章後，將申請書送至系辦，始得進行學位考試。
六、 本辦法經系務會議通過後於 109 學年度開始施行，修正辦法時亦於系務會議通過。

Date 2026-05-15

Dear Students,

To cultivate talents who promote mutual understanding between Taiwan and Japan, the Morito Institute of Global Higher Education at Hiroshima University will conduct the "2026 Summer Hiroshima University Japanese Language and Japanese Culture Special Program" during the upcoming summer vacation. The program currently offers the following two sessions:

Advanced Course: Thursday, July 16, 2026 – Friday, July 31, 2026

Standard Course: Thursday, July 2, 2026 – Wednesday, July 15, 2026

This program is planned to be held in person. For a detailed itinerary, please refer to the attached schedule.

I. Eligibility Criteria

Current undergraduate students in their sophomore year or above who have an interest in Japanese culture.

Applicants must be able to enroll in overseas travel insurance.

II. Application Procedure Please prepare the following documents: (a) Recommendation List (To be filled out by the Department Office) (b) Application Form (Attached Excel file; there are two types of forms, please ensure you select the correct one) (c) Photocopy of Passport (If you have not yet obtained a passport, please submit it immediately upon receipt) (d) ID Photo (A recent photo taken within the last month; please submit an electronic file such as JPEG) (e) Academic Transcript for All Semesters (English version required; single-semester transcripts are not accepted)

For the Advanced Course: Please email documents (b)-(e) to japanese@nccu.edu.tw by 4:00 PM on Thursday, June 11. Email Subject: Application for 2026 Summer Hiroshima University Japanese Language and Culture Special Program (① Advanced Course).

For the Standard Course: Please email documents (b)-(e) to japanese@nccu.edu.tw by 4:00 PM on Friday, May 29. Email Subject: Application for 2026 Summer Hiroshima University Japanese Language and Culture Special Program (② Standard Course).

III. Fees

Advanced Course: Fees payable to Hiroshima University (A)+(B): (A) Program Fee: 96,000 JPY; (B) Accommodation and Cleaning Fee: approx. 20,000 - 25,000 JPY.

Standard Course: Fees payable to Hiroshima University (A)+(B): (A) Program Fee: 72,000 JPY; (B) Accommodation and Cleaning Fee: approx. 20,000 - 25,000 JPY.

Additional self-funded expenses: (1) Round-trip airfare and local transportation in Japan, (2) Meals, (3) Overseas travel insurance, (4) Passport and visa application fees, (5) Personal transportation and souvenir expenses, etc.

Note: Each university may nominate a maximum of 5 students. If the minimum enrollment (5 students) is not met, the program may not be held. Students may choose the appropriate course based on their own circumstances. We encourage you to consider this opportunity carefully and apply enthusiastically.

The schedule for new students' credit transfer applications is as follows:

Master's and Doctoral Programs (including In-Service Master's Programs): August 10, 2026 (Mon) to August 13, 2026 (Thu), daily from 9:00 AM to 12:00 PM and 2:00 PM to 4:00 PM.

Undergraduate Freshmen (including Transfer Students): August 17, 2026 (Mon) to August 21, 2026 (Thu), daily from 9:00 AM to 12:00 PM and 2:00 PM to 4:00 PM.

To submit a credit transfer application, students must bring the relevant forms and documents directly to their respective department or institute office. Applications will not be accepted outside of working hours, during university summer holidays, on public holidays, or after the deadline.

Required Documents for Credit Transfer Application:

Credit Transfer Application Form (Please do not print double-sided).

One original copy of the official Chinese transcript of all academic years from the previous school graduated or attended.

When applying for general education credit transfers, or when deemed necessary by the department, please additionally attach the course syllabus from the semester/academic year the course was taken at the original school. (Must be attached!)

Course Credit Verification Form: If you have already obtained a degree from your previous school/department and wish to apply for credit transfer using courses you passed during that period that were not counted toward your degree, please fill out this form and have it verified by the authorized unit of your previous school.

Date 2025-08-12

Application Open until September 12

Eligibility Requirements:

Applicants must be:

	① Undergraduate students in their 2nd, 3rd, or 4th year in the Department;

	② Double-major students who have completed at least 16 required credits in the Department (excluding transferred credits);

	③ Master's program students in their 1st or 2nd year.

Returning students in their 5th undergraduate year or 3rd master's year after studying in Japan for one year.

A conduct grade of A and a GPA of 80 or above in the previous semester, with no failing grades.

Active participation in international exchange activities, Japanese-related competitions (on or off campus), or outstanding service contributions.

Must be enrolled in courses offered by the Department in the previous semester.

Ineligible Applicants:

Those who are scheduled to study abroad for over one month during the scholarship period.

Those with full-time employment income at the time of selection.

Those with full-time employment income during the scholarship period.

Required Application Documents (submit hard copies to the Department Office by the application deadline):

Scholarship application form (see attachment).

Official transcript of all academic records.

Undergraduate students: a study plan for the scholarship period.

	Master’s students: a research plan plus three course reports.

Other supporting documents for review (e.g., language proficiency certificates, volunteer service proof, award certificates, etc.).

For further details, please refer to the Nitori International Scholarship at National Chengchi University Regulations.

mother was a national of the Republic of China at the time of death.

be ascertained or both were stateless persons.

1.5. 審查程序 Application Review Process
外國學生入學申請，申請人應依本校招生簡章規定，於指定期間向本校國際合作事務
處提出申請。本處就申請人國籍及學歷是否符合外國學生身分進行初審；初審合格送
各系所複審；經各系所或學程審查合格者再交由審查小組審查之。前項審查小組由業
務主管副校長、教務長、國合長、各相關學院院長及相關系所或學程主管組成，並由
副校長召集之。審查合格者，由校長核定後，發給入學許可，通知入學。
Applicants should follow the regulations outlined in NCCU admissions brochure and submit
their applications to the Office of International Cooperation (OIC) within the designated
period. The office conducts an initial review of the applicants' nationality and educational
background to determine their eligibility as international students. Those who pass the initial
review will proceed to the department-level review conducted by respective departments or
programs. Candidates who are approved by the departments or programs will then be
forwarded to the admissions committee for further evaluation.
The admissions committee is composed of the Vice President in charge of international
affairs, the Dean of Academic Affairs, the Vice president for International Cooperation, the
deans of relevant colleges, and the directors of relevant departments or programs. The
committee is convened by the Vice President. Once the applicants pass the review, their
admissions will be approved by the President, and they will be issued an admission letter,
notifying them of their acceptance.

申請不限一系/所/學程，但僅能擇一系所學程辦理報到及註冊入學。

enroll in one department/graduate institute or program.

set up by individual departments/graduate institutes or program, such as additionally requested
application materials, oral tests, written tests, etc., and provide required documents.

系所名額得互為流用。
The admission quota of each department and graduate institute includes the admission quota
of ICDF scholarship applicants. The admission quota can be reallocated by the Admission
Committee if necessary.

使用語言相同之大學部語文課程。
According to article 2 of NCCU’s Guidelines for Restrictions on Studying Foreign Language
Courses, international students enrolled in the school are not allowed to take undergraduate
foreign language courses which are the official languages of their countries or other languages
that are their native languages.
(5) 依教育部規定，外國學生來臺就學後，其於就學期間許可在臺初設戶籍登記、戶籍遷
入登記、歸化或回復中華民國國籍者，喪失外國學生身分，應予退學；外國學生經入
學學校以操行、學業成績不及格或因犯刑事案件經判刑確定致遭退學者，不得再依
「外國學生來臺就學辦法」申請入學。違反規定經查證屬實者，取消其入學資格。
According to the regulations of the MOE (Ministry of Education), those who have been
approved to make Initial Household Registration, Moving-in Registration, or Acquisition or
Restoration of Nationality during their study in Taiwan and have thus ceased to possess the
status as foreign students, shall be dismissed from any school they are attending. Moreover,
those who withdraw or are dismissed from school in the Republic of China due to misbehavior,
unacceptable academic performance or a conviction under Criminal Law may thereafter not
apply again for admission under “Regulations Regarding International Students Undertaking
Studies in Taiwan.” Violation of the regulations, once confirmed, will result in the cancellation
of an application for admission.

to the Office of International Cooperation (OIC) within 14 days after the announcement of
the admissions results. The written statement should include the following information:
Name of the applicant, the department/program/graduate institute he/she applied to,
Address, Phone Number, Date of Appeal, and a statement of specific reasons and supporting
evidence for the doubt.
OIC should provide a formal response within one month of receiving the complaint and
should form a task force for an impartial investigation if necessary. If students are
unsatisfied with the outcome of the appeal to OIC, they may seek an administrative remedy
in accordance with the law.

Bureau of Consular Affairs, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, or Taiwan Overseas
Representative Offices can approve a visa. Some Taiwan Overseas Representative Offices may
require the applicants to submit proof of Chinese Language Proficiency (enrolling in Chinese-
taught programs) or proof of English Language Proficiency (enrolling in English-taught
programs) for their visa application. For the requirements of a visa application, please contact
the Taiwan Overseas Representative Office in/near your country. Please note that non-degree
students cannot apply for a visa with the purpose of studying.

1.5. 審查程序 Application Review Process
外國學生入學申請，申請人應依本校招生簡章規定，於指定期間向本校國際合作事務
處提出申請。本處就申請⼈國籍及學歷是否符合外國學生⾝分進行初審；初審合格送
各系所複審；經各系所或學程審查合格者再交由審查小組審查之。前項審查小組由業
務主管副校⻑、教務⻑、國合⻑、各相關學院院⻑及相關系所或學程主管組成，並由

Applicants should follow the regulations outlined in NCCU admissions brochure and submit
their applications to the Office of International Cooperation (OIC) within the designated
period. The office conducts an initial review of the applicants' nationality and educational
background to determine their eligibility as international students. Those who pass the initial
review will proceed to the department-level review conducted by respective departments or
programs. Candidates who are approved by the departments or programs will then be
forwarded to the admissions committee for further evaluation.
The admissions committee is composed of the Vice President in charge of international
affairs, the Dean of Academic Affairs, the Vice president for International Cooperation, the
deans of relevant colleges, and the directors of relevant departments or programs. The
committee is convened by the Vice President. Once the applicants pass the review, their
admissions will be approved by the President, and they will be issued an admission letter,
notifying them of their acceptance.

Date 2025-07-17

For [Course Search System](https://qrysub.nccu.edu.tw/) 

1.  When selecting sourses, students are advised not to focus solely on the course catefories, such as "required" or "program-specific" courses. Instead, attention should be given to the specific courses that  must be  completed in order to meet graduation requirements.

The list of required courses for each academic year can be found in the following locations.

[https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/zh/%E8%AA%B2%E5%8B%99%E7%B5%84/%E8%AA%B2%E7%A8%8B%E8%B3%87%E8%A8%8A](https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/zh/%E8%AA%B2%E5%8B%99%E7%B5%84/%E8%AA%B2%E7%A8%8B%E8%B3%87%E8%A8%8A)

If a course is listed as a "required" or "program-specific required" course in the curriculum for your year of admission, it means you must take and complete that course in order to graduate.

Conversely, if the course does not appear on the list, it is considered elective and may be taken at your discretion.

 

2. Starting from the 2018 academic year (Academic Year 107), the "Foreign Graduation Requirement" had been officially abolished.

 

Nevertheless, students are stronly encouraged to obtain JLPT N1 or N2 certification before graduation.

 

In addition, an important reminder for undergraduate students: Students of the College of Foreign Languages myst follow the university's English Selection refulations when enrolling in English Courses.

 

3.The implementation guidelines for the :Service-Learning and Practical Courses" at National ChengChi University were officially repealed starting from the 2020 academic year (Academic Year 109).

The proposal to abolish the zero-credit service-learning courses was approved during the 205th University Affairs Meeting on September 5, 2019.

As a result , Service-Learning courses are no longer classified as university- wide required courses.

They have been restructed as college- or department-specific courses, with relevant implementation measure approved at the first Academic Affairs Meeing of the second semester of the 2019-2020 academic year, held on March 30, 2020.

 

The repealed guidelines previously applied to the university-required "Service-Learning Courses," and they remained in effect only until the end of the 2019 acadamic year (Academic Year 108). The new policy has been in effect since the 2020 academic year (Academic Year 109).

 

4. Attention for Exchange Students:

If you plan to graduate in the same semester that your exchange program ends, please make sure to complete the following procedures within the specified deadlines to avoid any delays in your graduation schedule:

① Complete the credit transfer process before the one-third tuition refund deadline of the following semester.

※ This deadline, along with the tuition payment deadline, is noted in the University Academic Calendar each semester.

② For important information about the credit transfer process, please refer to:

[https://japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=2324&id=3805](https://japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=2324&id=3805)

 

5. Please note that the course selection FAQ is updated annually by the department office. Be sure to check the latest version down below.

[https://japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc?fid=2283](https://japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc?fid=2283)

 

 

The above information can be found on the NCCU website.

This summary has been provided for your convenience.

As these matters directly affect your academic progress and graduation eligibility, please read them carefully and do not overlook any details.

If students have any further questions after reviewing the information, feel free to contact the department office or the Office of the Academic Affairs, Registration.

Date 2026-07-09

【Departmental Courses】

Joint Undergraduate/Graduate Electives: The elective courses "Classical Japanese Grammar" (Course Code: 556894001), "Japanese-Chinese Literature and Its Intertwined Heritage" (Course Code: 556739001), and "Special Topics in Modern Japanese Political and Diplomatic History (3)" (Course Code: 556740001) are open jointly to both undergraduate and graduate students. Juniors and seniors who are interested are highly encouraged to enroll.

Summer Intensive Course: Although "Vietnamese Chinese Characters (Chữ Hán) and Cultural Exchanges in East Asia" is a joint undergraduate/graduate summer intensive course, its registration deadline was June 17 (Wednesday). Please note that no further course additions or drops will be accepted for this class.

Core Language Courses & Strict Capacity Caps: For the 2026 academic year, "Japanese Conversation Drill (I) & (II)" and "Japanese Composition (I) & (II)" will each be divided into three sections (Classes A, B, and C). Each section has a strict maximum capacity of 20 students. Any course addition petitions (overrides) will also be capped strictly within this 20-student limit; no over-enrollment will be permitted under any circumstances.

Automated Section Swapping Policy: Starting from the upcoming semester, the system will automatically swap sections (and consequently, instructors) for Class B of "Japanese Conversation Drill (II)," "Japanese Composition (I)," and "Japanese Composition (II)." To maintain an equal distribution of student numbers and language proficiency levels across the three sections, all Department of Japanese students (including double majors) are prohibited from dropping or changing their assigned sections, unless a special physical or mental health condition is verified and officially approved by the department.

Course Conflict Resolution: If you experience scheduling conflicts next semester and choose not to take "Japanese Conversation Drill (II)," "Japanese Composition (I)," or "Japanese Composition (II)," please complete the attached Course Drop Application Form and submit it to the Department Office by September 2 (Wednesday)(Digital copies are accepted; please email to japanese@nccu.edu.tw). Submissions after September 2 will not be processed by the department office; students must handle their own drop requests at the Registration Section during the official add/drop and petition period.

【Minor Program Courses】

Minimum Enrollment and Class Cancellation Policy: Starting from the 2024 academic year, all courses under the Minor Program must have a minimum of 20 enrolled students to officially run. Courses with fewer than 20 students will be canceled in two stages:

After the Add/Drop phase, if enrollment is below 16 students, the course will be canceled.

After the Course Petition (Addition/Withdrawal) phase, if enrollment is below 20 students, the course will be canceled. The Department Office will notify instructors and registered students once a cancellation is finalized. Students are strongly advised to monitor course enrollment numbers regularly.

Curriculum Adjustments & Course Substitutions:

"Japanese Reading (I) & (II)" apply strictly to students who declared their Minor in or after the 2024 academic year. Minor students who declared prior to the 2024 academic year must take "Intermediate Japanese" instead. Please refer to the "[Expanded Table of Course Substitutions for Minors](https://japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=2330&id=4104)" for full details.

For the 2026 academic year, the curriculum changes to Japanese Reading (I); "Elementary Japanese" will not be offered.

"Japanese Drill (I) & (II)" have been restructured into "Japanese Listening Practice" and "Advanced Japanese Listening Practice." Minor students registered prior to the 2024 academic year should use Japanese Listening Practice to waive Japanese Drill (I), and Advanced Japanese Listening Practice to waive Japanese Drill (II). (Credit waivers can be processed during your final graduating semester).

For any further inquiries regarding the Minor Program or for non-major students, please read the [Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)](https://japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=6180&id=41633)page thoroughly.

Date 2025-07-07

The elective course “Grammar of Ancient Japanese Literature” (Course Code: 556901001), offered by the Department, is a combined undergraduate and graduate-level course. Junior and senior undergraduate students who are interested are welcome to enroll.

For the 114 academic year, the following courses are divided into A/B/C classes, each with a maximum of 20 students:

Japanese Conversation & Listening (I)

Japanese Conversation & Listening (II)

Japanese Composition (I)

Japanese Composition (II)

In the 2nd semester, the classes for Japanese Conversation & Listening (II) ,Japanese Composition (II) and B Class of Japanese Composition (I)will be reassigned by the system (i.e., the instructors will be rotated). To ensure balance in class size and proficiency levels, Department of Japanese students (including double majors) are not allowed to request course withdrawals or class changes, unless there is a verified physical or mental health condition approved by the department.

If any scheduling conflict prevents students from taking the above-mentioned courses in the upcoming semester, they may submit a Course Withdrawal Request Form (see attached) by Aug. 28 (Thursday), either in person at the department office or via email to japanese@nccu.edu.tw.

After Aug. 28 , students must handle withdrawals themselves during the add/drop period through the Office of Academic Affairs.

Regarding Minor Program Courses:

Starting from the 113th academic year, all minor program courses require a minimum enrollment of 20 students (inclusive) to be offered. Courses with fewer than 20 students may be cancelled after the add/drop period, depending on the situation. The department office will notify the instructors once a course is confirmed to be cancelled. Students are advised to regularly monitor their course enrollment status.

The courses " Japanese Reading(1)" and " Japanese Listening" are required for students who declared the Japanese minor in AY 113.Those who declared the minor before AY 113 should instead take "Elementary Japanese" or " Studies in Japanese Language (1)/(2)".

The 114th academic year will be the final year for the Elementary Japanese course; starting from the 115th academic year, it will be restructured as “ Japanese Reading(1)”.

The courses “Studies in Japanese Language (1)” and “Studies in Japanese Language (2)” have been restructured as “Japanese Listening ” and “Advanced Japanese Listening.”

Students who declared a minor before the 113th academic year may use Japanese Listening to waive Studies in Japanese Language (1), and Advanced Japanese Listening to waive Studies in Japanese Language (2).

For questions regarding minor program courses, please refer to the [FAQ](https://japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=2283&id=5854).

Students from other departments are kindly asked to review the [FAQ](https://japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=2283&id=5853) as well.

Integration and Peace of East Asian Cultures

Good news! The application deadline has been extended to April 17 (Thursday).

If you’re interested, don’t miss out on this unique opportunity! The course will primarily be conducted in person.

Course Introduction

This course is a joint initiative among five departments from universities in Taiwan, Japan, and South Korea, combining overseas fieldwork in Japan with synchronous online lectures.

In commemoration of the 80th anniversary of the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Ceremony, the course explores cultural integration across East Asian countries and provides students with an opportunity for interdisciplinary, cross-cultural learning.

Course Details

Course Format: International Intensive Program

Credits: 2 credits

Main Instruction Language: Chinese (with Japanese and Korean support)

Teaching Style:In-person lectures held in Japan

Possible remote learning depending on circumstances

Intensive Course Period: August 24 (Sun) – August 28 (Thu), 2025

Location: Hiroshima University, Japan

Expenses: Students must cover their own travel and living costs, including airfare, accommodation, and daily expenses.

Important Notes for Course Registration

※ This intensive summer course is part of the Fall Semester 2025 (114-1).

Students who will be participating in exchange programs abroad during the 114-1 semester will not be eligible to earn credits for this course. Please do not register.

※ Once you register via the form below, the department will manually enroll you in the course. There is no need to add the course through the course selection system.

※ Graduate students who decide to withdraw from the course after attending will still be required to pay the credit fee.

※ If the number of applicants exceeds the enrollment limit, a selection process will be conducted.

※ This is a combined undergraduate–graduate level course. Therefore, first- and second-year undergraduate students are not eligible to register.

Date 2025-03-13

poster

Study Plan

Course Dates: March 19 (Wednesday) – March 26 (Wednesday), 2025 (Please refer to the detailed course schedule below)

Location: Department of Japanese Audiovisual Room

Total Instruction Hours: 36 hours

Credits: 2 credits

Eligible Students: Undergraduate and graduate students of the Department of Japanese, and Japanese international students enrolled at NCCU

Instructors:

Associate Professor  PING CHIEH YEH (Department of Japanese, National Chengchi University)

Professor Toshiyuki Sadanobu(Kyoto University, Japan; President of the Japanese Linguistic Society)

Language of Instruction: Japanese

Course Description:

This course studies the grammar of spoken Japanese through observation, aiming to master the fundamental concepts and principles of language. In the first half, the course explores grammar and speech context through aspects such as individuality, animacy, transitivity, and honorific expressions. Students will also learn distinctions between knowledge and experience, and rights in speech acts. The second half addresses the widely accepted concept that “conversation is a collection of sentences” (sentence-centrism), examining its limits and emphasizing the importance of basic speech forms such as words, sentences, phrases, non-autonomous speech units, primitive onomatopoeic expressions, and exclamations. Additionally, the course investigates emotional expression, power dynamics, and the naturalness of conversation influenced by these factors.

Please refer to the detailed syllabus for more information.

Class Size Limit: 15 students (undergraduate + graduate), plus 2 international students

Important Notes:

Students who are about to go on an exchange program cannot earn credits from this course and should not enroll.

Upon registration through this form, course enrollment will be handled by the department; students do not need to add this course via the online system.

Graduate students who wish to withdraw after attending must still pay tuition fees for the credits.

If enrollment exceeds the limit, students will be selected through a screening process.

This course is jointly offered to undergraduates and graduates; freshmen and sophomores are not eligible to enroll.

Date 2025-02-11

The course “International Course on Person Movement and Cultural Communication” (Course Code: 556750001), jointly offered for both undergraduate and graduate students, Students are welcome to enroll.

For the 113 academic year, the following courses are divided into A/B/C classes, each with a maximum of 20 students:

Japanese Conversation & Listening (I)

Japanese Conversation & Listening (II)

Japanese Composition (I)

Japanese Composition (II)

In the 2nd semester, the classes for Japanese Conversation & Listening (II)and Japanese Composition (II)will be reassigned by the system (i.e., the instructors will be rotated). To ensure balance in class size and proficiency levels, Department of Japanese students (including double majors) are not allowed to request course withdrawals or class changes, unless there is a verified physical or mental health condition approved by the department.

If any scheduling conflict prevents students from taking the above-mentioned courses in the upcoming semester, they may submit a Course Withdrawal Request Form (see attached) by February 11 (Tue.), either in person at the department office or via email to japanese@nccu.edu.tw.

After February 11, students must handle withdrawals themselves during the add/drop period through the Office of Academic Affairs.

Regarding Minor Program Courses:

The courses " Japanese Reading(1)" and " Japanese Listening" are required for students who declared the Japanese minor in AY 113.

Those who declared the minor before AY 113 should instead take "Elementary Japanese" or " Studies in Japanese Language (1)/(2)".

Please refer to the Substitute Course Table for Japanese Minor Requirements for more details.

⚠️ Please note: Students taking courses from the Japanese Department as part of a minor must pay full tuition, even when auditing. Refer to the “AY 113 Minor Program Tuition Policy” for details.

For more information about the minor program, please refer to the [FAQ](https://japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=2283&id=5854)for Japanese Minor Students on the department website.

To help outstanding high school graduates prioritize choosing the Department of Japanese as their top choice during the university application process, we encourage current students to share tips and experiences related to the second stage admission process, including document review and interview preparation. Early preparation and insights from senior students can be extremely helpful to incoming applicants!

1111 Job Bank is now collecting submission entries from current students of all departments, sharing their personal experiences in preparing application documents and interviews. These stories will support future applicants and help them succeed in joining the Department of Japanese!

 We encourage students from our department to participate—there’s a chance to win a cash prize!
