Date 2026-06-24

(Course Registration Notices: Please pay special attention to the highlighted content.)

※ Starting from the Fall Semester of the 113th Academic Year, credit fees will be reinstated for the Extended Minor program courses, and these courses will be open to all university students during the Add/Drop period. If a course is fully booked, students must assess the likelihood of successfully joining via the waitlist. (Please refer to the 113th Academic Year Extended Minor Fee Status Reference Table.)

※ "Japanese Seminar (I)" and "Japanese Seminar (II)" have been restructured into "Japanese Listening Practice" and "Advanced Japanese Listening Practice." Minor students enrolled before the 113th Academic Year should use Japanese Listening Practice to waive Japanese Seminar (I), and Advanced Japanese Listening Practice to waive Japanese Seminar (II).

※ The 114th Academic Year will be the final year "Elementary Japanese" is offered. In the 115th Academic Year, it will be restructured as "Japanese Reader (I)."

【Minor Students】

(1) What is the Extended Minor program? Originally, the quota for the minor program was quite limited (around 20-30 students). To meet university-wide demand, some departments increased their minor capacities. Our Department currently accepts 300 students (plus 5 from the UST system). Because this exceeds the teaching capacity of our internal faculty, the Extended Minor program primarily hires external instructors.

(2) Is the teaching quality of the Extended Minor program guaranteed? Every year, the Department conducts standard teaching evaluations and passes the unedited feedback to the instructors to help improve teaching quality. If students report any issues regarding the classes, we communicate them to the teachers. The evaluations also serve as a key reference for contract renewal. Over the past few years, students have highly praised the teaching quality of our instructors. We will strive to maintain this standard and encourage students to report any issues to the Department Office at any time.

(3) I am a new minor student. How and where do I register for courses? Please log into the university's course registration system. Under "Course Grouping and Department," select "General Education and Group Courses" (通識與分組開課) → "Minor" (輔系) → "Japanese Minor" (日輔). Please register for courses there (course codes start with 010), not under the main Department of Japanese. (Note: The course structure changes starting from the 113th Academic Year. Please refer to the Extended Minor Substitute Course List.)

(4) Are there any things I need to pay attention to when registering for courses?

Minor courses do not have prerequisite blocks (擋修). You may freely adjust your course schedule according to your situation. However, it is highly recommended to take courses sequentially as outlined in the minor course curriculum.

For full-year courses, if you do not pass the Fall semester, you will be blocked from taking the Spring semester. You can adjust your registration based on your academic progress and career planning, but we urge students to choose courses that match their actual Japanese proficiency level.

To take "Japanese Writing," students should possess language skills equivalent to at least having completed Elementary Japanese, and ideally possess Intermediate Japanese proficiency or higher. (Instructors have recently noted varying proficiency levels affecting teaching quality, so minor students are urged to take note).

(5) I previously took Japanese courses offered by the university. Now that I am an Extended Minor student, can I use these credits for waivers? For details, please refer to the "Minor Required Course List" under "Course Information" → "Undergraduate Program" on the Department website. To apply for a waiver, please complete the "Credit Substitution Application Form" (downloadable from the Department website → "About Us" → "Regulations & Forms" → "Student Forms") and submit it to the Department Office before graduation.

(6) I already have a foundation in Japanese and don't want to take the basic courses. What should I do? For the course skipping (advanced placement) policy, please refer to the Department website → "About Us" → "Regulations & Forms" → "Rules & Regulations." For every credit you skip, you must take an equivalent number of credits in Department elective courses to make up for it. For example, if you skip Elementary Japanese (6 credits), you must add 6 credits of Japanese Department electives. To apply, complete the "Credit Substitution Application Form" before graduation and submit it to the Department Office along with the original and a photocopy of your Japanese proficiency test certificate.

(7) What is the maximum number of credits I can waive?

For minor students enrolled in or before the 112th Academic Year: The maximum waiver limit is 16 credits (Required courses: up to 12 credits; Elective courses: up to 4 credits). This limit includes credits waived from study abroad programs.

For minor students enrolled from the 113th Academic Year onwards: The maximum waiver limit is 14 credits (Required courses: up to 10 credits; Elective courses: up to 4 credits). This limit includes credits waived from study abroad programs.

(8) What's the difference between Waiving, Skipping, and Substituting? Does it mean if I don't take certain courses, I have to take others? There are two scenarios:

If you are using university courses you've previously taken (whether offered by the Law Department or the FLC) to waive (抵免) credits, you can obtain your minor qualification with fewer remaining credits (deducting Elementary/Intermediate levels). Any further elective courses you take in the department are just for your own enrichment.

If you are applying for Credit Substitution (替代) (i.e., skipping (跳修) courses using an external proficiency certificate), you must take Department elective courses to make up for the credits of Elementary Japanese / Intermediate Japanese / Japanese Seminar (I). (Rule of thumb: The number of credits you skip must be exactly replaced by an equal number of elective credits.)

(9) I am a minor student, but I can't register for the minor course I want. What should I do? The Department has already opened many additional sections for the Extended Minor program. We ask students to try and adjust their course schedules. To maintain the teaching quality of each class, we advise against trying to force-add into a class that is already at full capacity.

(10) What does "Elective Courses" mean in the Minor Required Course Table? This refers to the core elective / elective courses offered to 3rd and 4th-year majors in the Department of Japanese (including Master's courses open to juniors and seniors). Only the elective courses listed in the Minor Required Course Table can be counted as minor elective credits. Elective courses not listed in this table will not be accepted as minor elective credits.

(11) I am a minor student, but I want to abandon my minor qualification. What should I do? Are the credits I've taken still useful? You must apply for abandonment online within the period specified by the university. (Please note: If you do not officially abandon it, you will not be able to graduate). Whether the credits you have already earned can be counted toward your graduation requirements will depend on your situation and your major department's regulations. Online Application Path: Log into iNCCU → University Info System Web Portal → Student Information System → Academic Services → "Apply/Abandon Minor & Double Major System." If you fail to abandon the minor within the standard timeframe and need to do so due to special circumstances, you must submit a special petition for approval.

(12) Starting from the 113th Academic Year, minor courses require a minimum of 20 enrolled students to open. Courses with fewer than 20 students will be canceled after the Manual Add/Drop period.

After the standard Add/Drop period, courses with 15 or fewer students will be canceled so that students in those courses can manually add other courses during the Manual Add/Drop phase.

After the Manual Add/Drop phase, courses with fewer than 20 students will be officially canceled. Students are advised to monitor enrollment numbers and check the Department website announcements regularly.

(13) The Department's courses do not allow for the printing of Course Add Forms. How can I manually add a course? The printing of Course Add Forms from the university system is disabled for all courses in the Department. Please go to the Department's website → "About Us" → "Regulations & Forms" → "Student Forms" to download the add form.

(14) What should I do if a course is blocked (擋修)? If you did not take the Fall semester of a full-year course and want to take the Spring semester course but are blocked by the system, there are two solutions:

Submit an application form during the "Permit Course Registration for Blocked Subjects" period, then register online yourself.

Submit a signed Course Add Form during the Manual Add/Drop period.

(15) I have other questions! Please contact the Department Office via email (japanese@nccu.edu.tw).

Q: I am a senior. If I am not admitted to the minor program, I am worried that I won't have enough time to complete the school-leaving (graduation) procedures. A: Please do not worry. You can still complete the school-leaving procedures in July. For more details, please contact the Registration Section.

Q: I am a senior. If I am admitted to the minor program and need to apply for study abroad course selection, I am worried that I won't have enough time to process the application. A: Please do not worry. The deadline for study abroad course selection applications is before the end of the Manual Add/Drop period of the following semester. For more details, please contact the Office of International Cooperation (OIC).

Q: When will the double major/minor admission results be announced? I am so anxious waiting every day that I log into iNCCU ten times a day. A: The Department hears your concerns and will expedite the process. However, because the number of applicants varies each year, the overall processing time may differ slightly. Please rest assured that the admission list will definitely be announced before the end of June.

Q: Why was my application rejected with a top 45% class rank, while my friend was accepted with a 48% rank? A: Please refer to the admission criteria: Students who meet the application standards are ranked based on their overall academic average from the previous semester, categorized by their respective colleges. The Department calculates the quota of admitted students for each college based on the proportion of applicants from that college. Therefore, the minimum percentage rank required for admission will naturally vary between different colleges.

(Course Registration Notices: Please pay special attention to the highlighted content.)

【Exchange Students】 (Including Double Major / Minor Exchange Students)

(1) I am going abroad! What should I pay attention to?

Please refer to the Office of International Cooperation (OIC) website and make sure to complete all necessary procedures:

Pre-departure Preparation: [https://oic.nccu.edu.tw/Post/291](https://oic.nccu.edu.tw/Post/291)

Returning Preparation: [https://oic.nccu.edu.tw/Post/292](https://oic.nccu.edu.tw/Post/292)

Alumni Experience Sharing: [https://oic.nccu.edu.tw/Category/579](https://oic.nccu.edu.tw/Category/579)

Once you are selected by a host university, regardless of whether you are ultimately able to go abroad, you MUST submit the "Course Selection Application for Study Abroad" to complete the administrative procedures. Failure to do so is equivalent to forfeiting your exchange student status. (The intended elective subjects must be filled out; do not leave them blank.) The Department Office will assist department majors with submitting the application. Submissions are collected centrally before the end of June and the end of December (announcements will be made in the departmental Facebook group).

If you complete the study abroad course selection procedures before the university tuition payment deadline, you can have your registration fee bill updated in advance. Otherwise, you must pay the registration fee first and apply for a refund after the procedures are completed.

Please review your currently uncompleted required and core elective courses. When selecting courses abroad, prioritize those that are similar or related to these required courses so that you don't spend a year abroad without being able to waive any required/core elective credits.

All credits earned in Japan, even if they cannot be used to waive required/core elective credits, can be counted as general elective credits. This applies regardless of whether our Department offers the course or if it's currently open this semester. However, please note that credits MUST be recorded on your official transcript to be waived. Courses that offer no credits and only issue a certificate of attendance cannot be used for credit waivers.

To waive required/core elective courses, you MUST keep the course syllabus, handouts, and your class notes. These are strictly necessary to process the credit waiver; without them, the waiver cannot be granted.

Three Core Principles for Planning Course Waivers Before Going Abroad:

Primarily Plan for Waiving Required Courses: Credit waiver planning should focus primarily on required courses. Waivers for required courses are reviewed by the Department Office or the relevant course instructors. (Minor required courses are reviewed by the Department Office).

For core elective course waiver guidelines, please refer to: [https://japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=2324&id=3805](https://japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=2324&id=3805)

Japanese elective courses are reviewed by the Department Office. (For elective courses, only a simple course syllabus is required, but you MUST provide one).

Match Field for Field: The content of the course taken abroad must be highly relevant to the content of the course you wish to waive.

Match Credit for Credit: You can use a higher number of credits to waive a lower number of credits, but not vice versa. If a subject has too few credits, you must take additional courses in the same field to accumulate enough credits. If the course taken does not use a credit system on the transcript, you may use teaching hours for the waiver. Similarly, you must use more hours to waive fewer hours. (Note: Courses that only provide a certificate of attendance cannot be used for credit waivers).

(2) I've heard that applying for credit waivers after returning to Taiwan is very troublesome. Is that true? Please follow the steps below, and the process will be quite straightforward:

I. Upon your return, you must present the following documents for verification by the Department Office and approval/signature by the Department Chair before credits can be waived:

"NCCU Student Application Form for Credit Waiver for Study Abroad" (see attachment, and refer to the provided example).

"Course Syllabus," "Teaching Materials/Handouts," "Class Notes," "Final Report," or "Other materials" (Mandatory for required/core elective courses; for elective courses, only the "Course Syllabus" is required).

"Official Transcript" (Mandatory; a temporary electronic copy is acceptable).

II. After the "Credit Waiver Application Form" is signed and approved by the Department Office and Department Chair, you must personally submit the following documents to the Curriculum Section / Registration Section:

"NCCU Student Application Form for Credit Waiver for Study Abroad"

"Official Transcript" (A photocopy is acceptable initially).

Important Notices!!

Students must submit their credit waiver applications before the 1/3 mark of the semester following their study abroad period (refer to the University Academic Calendar). If you do not intend to waive any credits, you MUST submit the "Affidavit for Forgoing Study Abroad Credit Waiver" (see attachment).

You may attach a photocopy of your transcript first, but you must provide the university with the original copy later.

The credit waiver process requires students (or a designated relative/friend) to submit the documents in person. Please do not send them by mail. We appreciate your understanding.

Credit waivers for elective courses are verified solely by the Department Office; instructor approval is not required.

All credit waiver approvals are evaluated based on the supporting documents provided for the actual courses taken, which must be submitted upon your return.

You can apply for waivers after returning, but you must bear the risk of a waiver being "denied." (If you are concerned, please consult with the Department Office or the relevant instructor beforehand).

Students opting not to waive any credits must still fill out the "Affidavit for Forgoing Study Abroad Credit Waiver" and attach their transcript.

Please pay close attention to the deadlines for all application items and try to complete your document submission and application procedures as early as possible. There are often cases where students rush to submit applications on the final day, encounter unexpected issues, and fail to smoothly process their exchange or waivers. To protect your own rights, please be mindful of all deadlines. (Please try your best to avoid submitting documents on the very last day!!!!)

(3) I have other questions! Please contact the Department Office via email (japanese@nccu.edu.tw).

Date 2026-06-24

(Course Registration Notices: Please pay special attention to the highlighted content.)

【Double Major Students】

(1) How should I register for courses?

Please register for courses under the Department of Japanese. The registration rules are identical to those for department majors. (Your curriculum year corresponds to your application year. For example, if you applied for the double major in the 113th AY, follow the 113th AY curriculum; if you applied in the 112th AY, follow the 112th AY curriculum → e.g., applying in the Spring semester of the 112th AY applies to the 113th AY curriculum). For course rules, refer to the Department website → "Course Information" → "Undergraduate Program" or the university website.

Please manually add required courses according to your personal study plan. Because the class schedules of the students' primary major departments vary greatly, the system cannot predict schedule conflicts with our Department's required courses, and therefore the Department will not automatically enroll you in them.

For sectioned courses like Japanese Conversation Seminar and Japanese Composition, double major students must manually choose a section with available spots.

Since the 108th AY, "Japanese Conversation Seminar (I) & (II)" and "Japanese Composition (I) & (II)" are divided into three sections. For the Fall semester, please add a section that is "not yet full."

Starting from the 114th AY, students in Japanese Conversation Seminar (I) and Japanese Composition (I) will not switch sections (except for Composition Section B). However, Japanese Conversation Seminar (II) and Japanese Composition (II) will require switching sections between semesters.

To maintain equal student numbers and proficiency levels across the three sections, double major students are not permitted to drop and switch sections in the Spring semester without special physical or mental health reasons and explicit departmental approval.

(2) Why can't I drop small class courses?

To maintain equal student numbers and proficiency levels across the three sections of our small class courses {Japanese Conversation Seminar (I)/(II), Japanese Composition (I)/(II)}, they are set as "non-droppable." If you have specific, justifiable reasons, you may apply to drop the course before the Add/Drop period begins (please see the latest news/course announcements). Please note that once you drop the course, you may not re-add the exact same course later.

(3) I previously took Japanese courses offered by the university. Now that I am a double major, can I use these credits for waivers?

Double majors are treated exactly as department majors. Please refer to the credit waiver regulations for department majors. (Due to different curriculum designs, minor courses cannot be used to waive major courses).

(4) Can I apply for course skipping (Advanced Placement)?

For the course skipping policy, please refer to the Department website → "About Us" → "Regulations & Forms" → "Rules & Regulations." For every credit you skip, you must make it up with an equal number of credits from the Department's elective courses. (Original certificates must be provided as proof).

Once you confirm you have made up the credits, submit the "Credit Substitution Application Form" to the Department Office before graduation. (Refer to the attached example for filling out the form).

(5) The required/core elective courses offered by the Department of Japanese keep conflicting with the courses in my original major.

We apologize for the inconvenience. We must consider many factors, such as instructors' availability and university regulations. Given the sheer volume of courses a double major student must take, it is practically impossible for every class to align perfectly without conflicts (if it does, congratulations!). Since you chose to pursue a double major, we trust you are mentally prepared for the possibility of delaying graduation by a year or two. We can only advise you to squeeze out all available time and complete the required courses as early as possible.

The Department Office has noticed an increasing number of students attempting to cram two years' worth of our Department's required courses into a single year. This approach is very risky because we cannot guarantee that the schedules for required courses across different years will not conflict. We strongly encourage students to take courses steadily and avoid leaving them until the very end, as the Department Office will be unable to assist if insurmountable conflicts arise.

(6) The Department's courses do not allow for the printing of Course Add Forms. How can I manually add a course?

The printing of Course Add Forms from the university system is disabled for all courses in the Department (both major and minor). Please go to the Department's website → "About Us" → "Regulations & Forms" → "Student Forms" to download the add form.

(7) If Elementary/Intermediate/Advanced Japanese conflicts with my major's schedule, can I take the Minor versions of Elementary/Intermediate/Advanced Japanese instead?

No. The curriculum design and credit structure for minor courses differ from major courses. Double major students must prioritize the courses offered for the major. (Note: Watch out for course codes starting with 506).

(8) What does "Double Major Transferring to Minor" (雙轉輔) mean?

If you are unable to complete the double major requirements, you may consider transferring it to a minor. However, this means applying to change your graduation status from "Double Major Qualification" to "Minor Qualification," which must be done before graduation.

Therefore, you must ensure you have earned enough credits to qualify for the minor (32 credits applicable before the 112th AY, or 28 credits applicable from the 113th AY onwards). Submitting the application does not immediately grant you minor status or the right to register via the minor system. Since you still hold double major status, it is recommended to prioritize taking the major's required courses. If you wish to take minor courses, you must select sections with available spots during the Add/Drop period and add them manually via the instructor's consent. Note: Starting from the Fall Semester of the 113th Academic Year, credit fees will be reinstated for the Extended Minor program courses.

Application Timeline for Transferring: Students must submit the application before the 2/3 mark of their expected graduation semester (please refer to the University Academic Calendar). Late applications will not be processed.

(10) What is the procedure for Double Major Transferring to Minor?

You must fill out the "Application Form for Student Abandoning Double Major to Transfer to Minor" (printed from the system) and the "Credit Substitution Application Form" (detailing which major courses you are using to waive the minor courses).

We recommend prioritizing double major courses, and then processing waivers to obtain your minor qualification.

Procedure for applying to take minor courses: During the Add/Drop period, email the Department Office indicating the minor course you wish to take → The Department Office will seek the instructor's consent → Have the instructor sign the Course Add Form during the Manual Add/Drop phase.

Submission Deadline: Students must submit the application before the 2/3 mark of their expected graduation semester (please refer to the University Academic Calendar). Late applications will not be processed.

(11) I am double majoring in the Department of Japanese. Can I apply to graduate with the Department of Japanese as my primary degree?

Absolutely. According to Article 10, Paragraph 2 of the University's Regulations for Undergraduate Double Majors: "In the semester of expected graduation, a student pursuing a double major who has completed the required course credits for the double major, met the graduation requirements of that department, and obtained the qualification of the original department (Department of Japanese), may submit a special petition to graduate with the double major department as their primary degree. The application deadline follows the schedule for abandoning a double major or minor." Therefore, this application has been available since the Spring Semester of the 109th Academic Year.

Please note that if a student wishes to graduate with their double major as their primary degree, in addition to completing the required credits and meeting the graduation conditions of the double major department, they must also fulfill the minor qualifications of their original department.

Furthermore, students must submit the application before the 2/3 mark of their expected graduation semester (please refer to the University Academic Calendar).

Required documents for submission: Application Form (see attachment) + Complete Academic Transcript.

(12) Will courses be blocked (擋修)?

Although the Department's courses generally do not have prerequisites, for full-year courses, if you fail to take the Fall semester, the system will block you from adding the Spring semester course. In this case, you must submit a petition to override the block. Please refer to the attachment for the application procedure.

(13) I am a double major student, but I want to abandon my double major qualification. What should I do? Are the credits I've taken still useful?

You must officially apply for abandonment online within the period specified by the university. (Please note: If you do not officially abandon it, you will not be able to graduate). Whether the credits you have already earned can be counted toward your graduation requirements will depend on your situation and your major department's regulations.

Online Application Path: Log into iNCCU → University Info System Web Portal → Student Information System → Academic Services → "Apply/Abandon Minor & Double Major System."

If you fail to abandon the double major within the standard timeframe and need to do so due to special circumstances, you must submit a special petition for approval.

(14) I have other questions!

Please contact the Department Office via email (japanese@nccu.edu.tw).

(Course Registration Notices: Please pay special attention to the highlighted content.)

【General Questions / Non-Majors】

(1) How do course capacity settings and course categories (Required, Core Elective, Elective) work? Course Capacity Settings:

Required courses offered by the Department of Japanese are strictly closed to non-majors for enrollment or auditing. Double major students are treated as department majors.

Elective courses offered by the Department are open to all university students.

Minor students (including Extended Minor students) may enroll in specific elective courses (refer to the Extended Minor Substitute Course List) and core elective courses offered by the Department via the registration system.

Starting from the 113th Academic Year, the Extended Minor courses will only be open to non-majors if there are remaining spots available (degree program students can only register for specific courses). Please add these courses during the Add/Drop period. Note: Starting from the Fall Semester of the 113th Academic Year, credit fees will be reinstated for the Extended Minor program courses. Please refer to the tuition and fee standards. Summary: The most important thing is to know exactly which courses you must complete to graduate, earn a double degree, or obtain a minor/program certificate. As long as you have completed the required courses and met the relevant standards, we will recognize them regardless of their specific category.

(2) I really want to learn Japanese, but I wasn't admitted to the Extended Minor program (or I don't want to pay credit fees / I only want to take basic courses / I am a freshman). What should I do? Students can take Japanese courses through the following channels:

We recommend enrolling in Japanese courses offered by the Foreign Language Center (FLC) or the Center for Public and Business Administration Education (CPBAE).

During the Add/Drop period, you may enroll in minor courses that still have available spots. (Note: Minor courses require credit fees; the course code starts with 010).

(3) Why aren't there more Japanese courses open to all university students? Also, why aren't there more available spots? This is due to the strict limitations on the teaching hours of our faculty (according to university regulations, professors/associate professors/assistant professors cannot exceed 6 extra teaching hours). To maintain teaching quality and accommodate individual faculty research schedules, the capacity for each class varies. However, the Department has made great efforts to offer as many courses as possible to meet campus-wide demand and has significantly increased the quota for the Extended Minor program. Why offer these courses under the Extended Minor program instead of regular department courses? Is it to collect credit fees? The answer is no. Faculty compensation for the Extended Minor program is funded separately and is not restricted by university staffing quotas or standard teaching hour limits. This flexibility is what allows us to open more class sections.

(4) What elective courses are offered by the Department of Japanese this year? Elective courses are offered across the Fall and Spring semesters. For details, please check the University Course Catalog under "College of Foreign Languages and Literature" → "Undergraduate Program" → "Department of Japanese."

(5) The Department's courses do not allow for the printing of Course Add Forms. How can I manually add a course? The printing of Course Add Forms from the university system is disabled for all courses in the Department (both major and minor). Please go to the Department's website → "About Us" (系所介紹) → "Regulations & Forms" (規章表格) → "Student Forms" (學生相關) to download the Department's official Course Add Form.

(6) I have other questions! Please refer to the Q&As in other categories first. If your question is not answered, please contact the Department Office via email (japanese@nccu.edu.tw).

Date 2026-06-24

(Course Registration Notices: Please pay special attention to the highlighted content.)

【Department Majors】

(1) Is there a mistake? Why can't I register for our department's elective courses?

Please personally ask the course instructor if they are willing to allow you to manually add the course. If approved, submit the Course Add Form with the instructor's signature to the Department Office within the university's specified timeframe to process your registration.

The system printing of Course Add Forms is disabled for all courses in the Department of Japanese (both major and minor). Please go to the Department's website → "About Us" (系所介紹) → "Regulations & Forms" (規章表格) → "Student Forms" (學生相關) to download the Add Form yourself.

(2) Can I apply for course skipping (Advanced Placement)?

For the course skipping policy, please refer to the Department website → "About Us" → "Regulations & Forms" → "Rules & Regulations." Please note that no matter how many credits you skip, the total number of credits required for graduation remains exactly 128.

(For every credit skipped, you must make up for it with an equal number of credits from the Department's elective courses.)

Once you have confirmed you have made up the required credits, apply for course skipping by submitting the "Credit Substitution Application Form" along with the original and a photocopy of your JLPT certificate to the Department Office before graduation. (For an example of how to fill out the form, refer to the attachment).

(3) How should I choose sections for sectioned courses?

Since the 109th Academic Year, these courses have been divided into 3 sections, with students automatically assigned (system enrolled) by the Department. Starting from the 114th Academic Year, students in Japanese Conversation Seminar (I) and Japanese Composition (I) will not switch sections (except for Composition Section B). However, Japanese Conversation Seminar (II) and Japanese Composition (II) will require switching sections between the Fall and Spring semesters.

To maintain equal student numbers and proficiency levels across the three sections, Department majors (including double majors) are not permitted to drop and switch sections without special physical or mental health reasons and explicit departmental approval.

(4) Why can't I drop Japanese Conversation Seminar (I)/(II) and Japanese Composition (I)/(II)?

To maintain equal student numbers and proficiency levels across the three sections of our small class courses {Japanese Conversation Seminar (I)/(II), Japanese Composition (I)/(II)}, they are set as "non-droppable." If you have specific physical/mental conditions or schedule conflicts, you may apply to drop the course before the Add/Drop period begins (please see separate announcements). Please note that once you drop the course, you may not re-add the exact same course later.

(5) What if I am considering transferring departments or taking a leave of absence?

If you need to transfer departments or take a leave of absence due to personal reasons, we highly recommend that you inform and discuss your plans with your academic advisor first before applying at the Department Office. Thank you.

(6) Will extra core elective courses count as elective courses?

Yes. Once you have fulfilled the required number of core elective credits, any additional core elective courses you take will be counted as general elective credits.

(7) Will I face academic dismissal for failing half my credits (the "2/1" rule)?

Because Article 33 of the University Academic Regulations has been deleted, the "2/1" academic dismissal rule no longer exists. However, according to Article 50: Undergraduate students who fail to complete the required graduation credits within the prescribed study period may extend their study period by one semester to a maximum of two academic years. Therefore, please pay close attention to your graduation time limit. (This does not mean you can infinitely fail classes every semester!)

(8) I double major in Department XX. Can I apply to graduate with Department XX as my primary degree?

Absolutely. According to Article 10, Paragraph 2 of the University's Regulations for Undergraduate Double Majors: "In the semester of expected graduation, a student pursuing a double major who has completed the required course credits for the double major, met the graduation requirements of that department, and obtained the qualification of the original department (Department of Japanese), may submit a special petition to graduate with the double major department as their primary degree. The application deadline follows the schedule for abandoning a double major or minor." Therefore, this application has been available since the Spring Semester of the 109th Academic Year.

Please note that if an undergraduate student wishes to graduate with their double major as their primary degree, in addition to completing the required credits and meeting the graduation conditions of the double major department, they must also obtain the Minor qualification of the Department of Japanese.

Application Deadline: Students must submit the application before the 2/3 mark of their expected graduation semester (please refer to the University Academic Calendar).

Required Documents: Application Form (see attachment) + Credit Substitution Application Form + Academic Transcript.

The Department's minor qualification can be recognized and waived using the Department's major courses as follows:

Notes:

Department courses can only be used to waive minor courses when transferring from double major to minor, or when applying to graduate with the double major department as the primary degree. Because minor and major curricula differ, minor courses cannot be used to waive major courses.

When waiving credits, you can only use a higher number of credits to waive a lower number of credits; any surplus/leftover credits cannot be used to waive other subjects.

(9) Will courses be blocked (擋修)?

Although the Department's courses generally do not have prerequisites, for full-year courses, if you fail to take the Fall semester, the system will block you from adding the Spring semester course. You must submit an application for "Permit Course Registration for Blocked Subjects." Please refer to the attachment for the procedure.

Note: After your block-override application is approved, you must manually log into the system and add the course yourself.

(10) Can extra General Education credits count as elective credits?

No, extra General Education credits will not be counted towards your graduation credits. However, extra core elective credits can be counted as elective credits!

(11) Can I apply for early graduation?

Yes, if you meet the conditions below. However, early graduation requires discussion and approval at the Departmental Affairs Meeting. Therefore, ensure you submit your application to the Department Office within one month prior to the university's official deadline (which falls between the Manual Add/Drop deadline and the Course Withdrawal deadline each semester).

Your weighted average academic grade (excluding the semester of early graduation) must be 80 or above, OR you must rank within the top 20% of students in your department and grade level.

Your conduct grade for every semester must be 80 or above, or an A.

Because it must pass the Departmental Affairs Meeting, applicants are urged to submit their requests as early as possible.

Required Documents: Early Graduation Application Form (see attachment), Complete Academic Transcript, and Conduct Transcript.

(12) Do I need to apply for delayed graduation?

If you have not met the standard graduation credit requirements, or if you have unfulfilled credits for your minor or double major, you will automatically be classified as a delayed graduation student. No special application is required.

(13) I have other questions!

Please contact the Department Office via email (japanese@nccu.edu.tw).

【Program Students】

(1) What courses can I actually take?

Currently, the Department supports the "Foreign Language Communication Second Specialty Program" and the "Translation and Cross-Cultural Program." For the specific courses open to program students, please refer to the university's system instructions or the course catalog.

(2) If I have previously taken Japanese courses offered by the university, can I directly waive credits?

Please refer to the "Minor Required Course Table" under "Course Information" → "Undergraduate Program" on the Department website.

Date 2026-06-24

【Master's Students】

(1) I would like to take courses offered by other departments at NCCU or at other universities. Is this allowed, and how do I apply? Yes, it is allowed. Please follow the "National Chengchi University Regulations for Domestic Inter-University Course Selection" and the "National Chengchi University Course Implementation Regulations."

The maximum number of credits you can take from other departments or other universities is capped at 7 credits.

You may take a maximum of 6 credits per semester from master's programs at other universities, and you must obtain prior approval from the Department before enrolling.

(2) I am a new student. How should I register for courses? Except for the university-mandated "Academic Research Ethics Education Course," the Department's Master's program currently has no required courses. Students may freely select courses. You can graduate after completing 28 credits and writing your thesis. For related regulations, we strongly recommend thoroughly reading the guidelines under "Course Information" → "Master's Program" on the Department website, as well as the "Regulations for Degree Study and Qualifying Examinations for Graduate Students in the Master's Program, Department of Japanese, National Chengchi University."

(3) What is the "Academic Research Ethics Education Course"? Master's students enrolled from the 105th Academic Year onwards must take and pass the Academic Research Ethics Education Course before the end of their first academic year. Students who fail to pass this course are not allowed to apply for the degree examination.

Course Format: Please take the 6-hour online course and complete the assessment on your own. If you fail the assessment, you must retake the online course. For course-related links, please refer to: Office of Academic Affairs → Registration Section → Academic Research Ethics Education Course Section.

The Registration Section will send out email notifications regarding course registration matters. If students have any related questions, please contact the Registration Section directly.

(4) Final Degree Examination Application Process Please refer to the following link for details: [https://japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageDownload?fid=2336](https://japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageDownload?fid=2336)

(5) What is the schedule for the day of the oral defense? What are the time limits for the presentation and the Q&A session? Please discuss the duration of your final oral defense presentation with your advisor. Past students have had presentations ranging from 20 to 30 minutes. There is no strict time limit for the Q&A session. Generally, the entire final oral defense takes about 2 hours.

(6) What documents do I need to prepare on the day of the defense (e.g., transcript confirmation, physical copies of the thesis)? The mandatory documents for the day of the defense include: the Oral Defense Score Sheet, the Committee Members' Signature Page, and the Electronic Thesis Academic Quality Agreement. You can prepare these in advance, or arrive early at the Department Office on the day of the defense to prepare them.

(7) Do I need to prepare refreshments for the committee members on the day of the oral defense? The Department Office does not encourage the culture of providing refreshments. However, different professors have different practices; please follow your advisor's guidance on this matter.

(8) I have other questions! Please ask senior students directly or contact the Department Office via email (japanese@nccu.edu.tw).

In response to the trend of globalization and to cultivate talents with multilingual abilities, the Department of Japanese Language and Culture at National Chengchi University has established the "Fundamental Japanese Micro-Program."

Date 2025-06-17

Q1: What areas of expertise do the professors at NCCU's Japanese Department specialize in?

A:

Our full-time faculty members specialize in three main areas, with a total of 9 professors:

Linguistics: 4 professors

Japanese Literature: 3 professors

Japanese History and Culture: 2 professors

This diverse structure allows students to explore the Japanese language and culture from multiple academic perspectives.

 

Q2: What do the linguistics professors teach? Is it difficult to understand?

A:

Not at all! Our linguistics professors cover a wide range of fields, from theoretical linguistics to sociolinguistics. Their teaching is clear and approachable, helping students:

Grasp the grammatical structure of Japanese

Compare it with Mandarin and other languages

You won’t just learn how to use the language—you’ll also understand how it works.

 

Q3: Does studying literature just mean reading old texts? What can I do with it?

A:

Not at all! Our literature professors specialize in everything from classical to modern and contemporary Japanese literature. Through literature, students gain insight into:

The psychology and social structures of Japanese people

The connections between literature and popular culture, such as anime and film

So if you're interested in stories, creativity, or Japanese media, this is the perfect path for you!

 

Q4: How is studying Japanese history and culture relevant?

A:

Our professors of history and culture are experts in both Japanese history and Japan–Taiwan cultural relations. Their courses help you:

Understand Japan’s historical and social development

Reflect on your own cultural identity through comparative studies

You’ll become someone who truly understands Japan—and your own roots.

 

Q5: Are there any practical or career-oriented courses in addition to academic ones?

A:

Absolutely! In addition to core academic courses, we offer a variety of practical elective courses, such as:

Business Japanese, to prepare you for professional environments

Japanese–Chinese Translation, to sharpen your language skills for further study or the job market

Whether your goal is graduate study or immediate employment, you’ll find a pathway that fits your future.

日文系擴大輔系課程有幾點注意事項如下：

2025.9.1加退選階段開放全校學生選課。若課程已額滿，請同學自行評估遞補成功的可能性。

關於112學年以前(含112)申請輔系的同學：

請留意「日語讀本一」與「日語讀本二」為113學年度起輔系生必修科目，112學年以前(含112)的輔系同學請選修「初級日語」與「中級日語」。

 114學年的「初級日語」為最後一堂初級日語，請112學年以前(含112)的輔系同學把握今年最後機會。

115學年度「中級日語」只剩一班，請112學年以前(含112)的輔系同學，今年若沒衝堂的話，趕緊將中級日語選起來。

「日語演習一」請以「日語聽力練習」抵免，「日語演習二」請以「進階日語聽力練習」抵免，以一堂課抵一堂課，而不是以一堂2學分的課抵二堂1學分的課。

關於113學年起申請輔系的同學：

請優先加選尚未額滿之班級，協助課程順利開課。(滿20人開課)

若選日文系本系選修課，隨班附讀也需收費，且是全額收費。詳見「擴大輔系恢復收費身分基準一覽表」。

日文系所有課程未開放加簽單列印，敬請至本系網站「系所介紹」→「規章表格」→「學生相關」下載加簽單。（加簽單請於加簽暨退課階段再送至系辦，提早送不受理）

每位老師加簽原則不同，有的老師是優先讓延畢生加簽，有的老師有其他優先順序，系上尊重任課老師的原則。

一、說明：

 

為凝聚系所認同、展現本系特色，國立政治大學日本語文學系特舉辦系徽LOGO徵稿活動，誠摯邀請本系同學及系友們一同發揮創意，為本系設計一款兼具象徵意義與視覺美感的專屬標誌！

作品設計應能體現本系核心理念，如「日文專業」、「文化交融」、「學術精神」與「國際視野」，並具現代感與辨識度，適用於本系各類公關宣傳與官網使用。

二、主辦單位：國立政治大學日本語文學系

三、參賽對象與資格：

本校日本語文學系／研究所學生（含雙主修，須具有效學籍者）以及本系畢業系友

每人限投稿一件作品。參賽作品必須為原創，且未曾公開發表、參加其他競賽，亦不得授權或轉讓予第三方。

四、徵稿內容與規範

(一) 作品內容須包含：

系徽 LOGO 設計稿

設計理念簡述（300字以內）

※ 若作品中包含系的文字，請統一使用以下版本：

中文：國立政治大學日本語文學系

英文：Department of Japanese Language and Culture

※ 鼓勵融入台灣或日本意象元素，但請避免使用過度常見圖像（如鳥居、富士山、櫻花等），以強調獨特性與創新性。

收件截止期限：114年10月31日(五)

其他事項請再詳閱附加檔「國立政治大學日本語文學系系徽LOGO徵稿」之內容，謝謝。

114學年度日文系擴大輔系獎學金即日起開放申請至10/3 12:00

9/30補公告:若同學依照輔系科目表，完成第一年建議之三門課程:日語讀本一、日語會話一、日語聽力練習，上下學期合計修滿12學分者，也可提出申請。

本獎學金申請資格為113學年度起新制之輔系生，詳細如下：

1. 修讀本系擴大輔系一學年以上。

2. 獎學金申請期間具擴大輔系生資格。

3. 前一學期修習本系擴大輔系課程達八學分、所屬課程總平均依照學分數進行加權計算至小數點第二位（四捨五入後）達八十八分以上，且無一科目不及格、棄修之學生。

 

申請者應檢具下列文件，10/3 12:00前紙本送至系辦(逾時不候)以備審核：

一、 獎學金申請單。

二、 歷年成績單。

其他詳細請參照「國立政治大學日本語文學系擴大輔系生獎學金申請辦法」

本獎學金之獎勵名額，由符合申請同學中，視該年實際收支情形，由學生事務委員會遴選若干名，報系務會議核備後決定。

 108年8月1日起，欲提出學位考試申請者，請依「國立政治大學研究生學位考試要點」第三條之第二款之申請程序提出申請：「研究生填具學位考試申請書，其論文經校內論文抄襲比對系統比對、送請指導教授簽名同意、系所完成畢業初審並經系所主管簽章後，將申請書送教務處複審同意後，始得進行學位考試。」。

　　另有關考試委員資格，請依要點第六、七條規定提聘，若為第六、七條之第三款、第四款資格之認定基準，由辦理學位授予之各系、所、院務會議或學位學程事務會議定之。

＊研究生請至【圖書館網頁/電子資源指南-資料庫/Turnitin學術論文原創性比對系統】申請三步驟：

1.申請帳號，請填寫表單

https://goo.gl/bThBmM (需一個工作天)

2.開通Turnitin帳號

請留意政大email，依照信件指引開通帳號。

3.上傳論文進行比對

*請點課程名稱進入課程主頁，點選「提交」即可比對。

*在作業有效期限內，均可重覆的提交文稿進行比對，提醒您! 提交第三次後須等 24 小時後才能產生新報告。

如若有相關疑問，可電洽圖書館推廣組分機77066/62641諮詢。

政學務字第1090002938號

主 旨：

由於本校因應嚴重特殊傳染性肺炎疫情延後至109年2月25日開學，檢送更新後之「109學年提前入學新生健康檢查須知」及「108學年度第二學期短期研修生健康檢查須知」相關事宜，請查照並轉知所屬。

登載日期：

109/02/07

登載期限：

109/02/14

承辦人員：

洪梅玲

承辦單位：

學生事務處身心健康中心

內 容：

一、依據「學校衛生法第八條」、「學校衛生法施行細則第6條」、「傳染病防治法第36條」及本校「學生健康檢查實施辦法」辦理。

			二、實施對象及體檢項目

			（一）109學年度碩士班、碩士在職專班提早於108學年第二學期入學之學生，請於109年2月3日(一)至3月10日(二)至啟新診所或合格公私立醫院完成教育部規定項目之健康檢查，相關說明請參閱「109學年度提前入學新生健康檢查須知」（附件一)。

			（二）來臺研習3個月以上且未滿6個月之外籍學生(不包括華語文生)、僑生、港澳學生，應完成短期研修停留健檢項目，相關說明請參閱短期研修生健康檢查須知（附件2）。本校短期研修生校內體檢辦理資訊如下：

			１、時間：109年2月24日(一)下午13：00-16：30

			２、地點：四維堂

			３、委辦單位：啟新診所

			４、辦理時段：

			（１）13：30-15：00 國合處外籍生

			（２）15：00-16：30 商學院及其他

日期：2026-03-06

「搭僑計畫」為僑務委員會推動的青年海外交流計畫，透過政府補助，讓國內大專學生赴海外參訪見習。今年計畫首度增設「日語組」，希望結合學生的語文專長與跨文化交流能力。

 

為讓更多同學有充裕時間獲知訊息並準備申請，本計畫報名截止延長至 3月13日（星期五）。

 

曾參與過的學生多表示，透過實地接觸海外僑界、當地政府及企業單位，對拓展國際視野與職涯探索都有很大的幫助。

 

＊在搭僑行程中，學生將有機會：

・直擊海外職場實況

・汲取前輩實戰經驗

・體驗跨國文化交流

・釐清未來職涯方向

・建立實質人脈連結

 

＊報名資格：18–30歲國內大專在學生（含碩博士），並具備規定之語言能力證明

 

＊截止日期：3/13(五)

日期：2026-03-18

都留文科大学位於日本山梨縣，為一所公立大學，並與世界多所大學建立交換合作關係，提供交換留學及短期語言研修等多元國際交流機會。本系已與該校簽訂交換留學合作計畫，歡迎同學踴躍申請參與，透過在日本的學習與生活體驗，拓展國際視野、深化日語能力，並提升未來發展的競爭力。

若有意願參加系級交換之同學，請參閱附件之都留文科大學環境介紹(Fact Sheet 2026 Fall アジア)。

申請條件

應具備日本語能力試驗 N2 以上之語言能力（未持有合格證書者，須附政治大學日本語文學系教師之推薦信）。

申請名額

交換期間可為一學期或一學年。交換人數原則上以一學期 4 名、一學年 2 名為限。

都留文科大學將提供下列協助事項：

a) 宿舍安排之協助

b) 日本入境相關手續之協助

c) 其他學習及生活支援事項

 

申請文件

日本語文學系系級薦外交換學生甄選報名表（如附檔）

歷年成績單

學習計畫（A4 不超過 2 頁）

日語能力檢定證明

其他補充資料（如系上各類活動與演講之參與證明等）

申請方式

	請將上述文件以 e-mail 寄至系辦信箱 japanese@nccu.edu.tw，

	或將紙本資料送至系辦公室。

招募截止日

	3 月 25 日

如經系上甄選通過，後續將由都留文科大學聯繫，並需準備相關申請文件（參照Fact Sheet 2026 Fall アジア，預計須於 4 月 10 日前 繳交）

日期：2020-06-10

發文字號：

政教字第1090015228號

主 旨：

公告本校108學年度學士班應屆畢業生集中離校相關事宜，請查照。

登載日期：

109/06/08

登載期限：

109/06/15

承辦人員：

施漢妤

承辦單位：

教務處註冊組

內 容：

一、108學年度學士班應屆畢業生集中離校茲訂於本（109）年7月2日（星期四）至3日（星期五），每日上午9時至下午4時30分止，於本校行政大樓四樓教務處第一及第二會議室集中辦理學位證書發放作業。

			二、依日前中央流行疫情指揮中心公布社交距離指引，請同學辦理離校進入公告事項一之場所時，由於無法維持室內1.5公尺之社交距離，請務必配戴口罩。

			三、學士班應屆畢業生，應先上網列印個人離校程序單（政大首頁→iNCCU→校務系統Web入口→學生資訊系統→學生畢業離校檢核）及攜帶學生證，至各處室辦理還清圖書、學士服等程序，最後經教務處審核符合畢業資格後，完成畢業離校手續，領取學位證書。若委託他人（含直系親屬）代辦者，須另附委託書([http://newdoc.nccu.edu.tw/formservice/44/44_3372.pdf)及雙方身分證件正本辦理](http://newdoc.nccu.edu.tw/formservice/44/44_3372.pdf)%E5%8F%8A%E9%9B%99%E6%96%B9%E8%BA%AB%E5%88%86%E8%AD%89%E4%BB%B6%E6%AD%A3%E6%9C%AC%E8%BE%A6%E7%90%86)。

			四、學士班應屆畢業生請先上網查詢當學期成績是否已到齊（政大首頁→iNCCU→校務系統Web入口→學生資訊系統→成績查詢），再行辦理畢業離校程序，執行畢業檢核並列印離校程序單，辦理離校事宜。惟離校程序單列印後，各項資源（圖書、畢業服、宿舍…等）之借用權益即時消滅。

			五、未及於7月2日至3日二天辦妥離校手續者，請於7月6日起，依前述作業程序，於上班時間完成各單位核章後，再至教務處註冊組領取學位證書。此外，7月8日本校舉辦109學年度轉學生入學考試，行政同仁支援考試業務，暫停服務，請避開當日前來辦理離校手續。

日期：2020-05-14

109學年度語言學研究所「語言、認知與大腦」跨領域學分學程，自即日起開始受理申請，敬請同學踴躍申請。

一、本學程提供的跨領域知識包含語言學、認知心理學、資訊科學及腦神經學，提供學生語言學、心理語言學、計算機語言學、語言與大腦知識，也介紹本校腦造影及眼動技術，以培養學生探究語言、認知與大腦的知能，進而具備跨領域的知識及從事跨領域研究的能力。

二、本學程招生對象為大學部二、三、四年級學生及碩士班一、二年級學生。

三、申請時間自即日起開始，至6月24日星期三截止。

四、申請表請見附件一，本學程施行細則（含修習學分及取得證書等相關規定）請見附件二。

五、本學程聯絡人：曾惠鈴助教，聯絡電話：02-29387246；學分學程相關資訊請見網頁：[http://ling.nccu.edu.tw/lcb/pages.php?ID=lcb1](http://ling.nccu.edu.tw/lcb/pages.php?ID=lcb1)。

text:
[:::](http:japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=2127&id=5349#accesskey-l)

[:::](http://japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=2127&id=5349#accesskey-c)

日期：2020-06-10

發文字號：

政學務字第1090014968號

主 旨：

為配合教育部政策，本校擬辦理109學年度畢業一、三、五年流向調查（本次調查對象為107、105、103學年度畢業之本國籍學生），惠請貴院、系、所通知前揭畢業校友於本校職涯發展與實習/志工平台（[https://cd.nccu.edu.tw）線上填寫訪查問卷，以增進畢業生流向完訪率，並可作為各系所評鑑、課程規劃與學生發展瞭解之參考依據，請查照](https://cd.nccu.edu.tw）線上填寫訪查問卷，以增進畢業生流向完訪率，並可作為各系所評鑑、課程規劃與學生發展瞭解之參考依據，請查照)。

登載日期：

109/06/08

登載期限：

109/06/15

承辦人員：

趙紀綱

承辦單位：

學生事務處職業生涯發展中心

內 容：

一、為配合高教深耕計畫持續提升本校畢業生流向完訪率，本校畢業生流向調查擬區分兩階段進行：

			（一）第一階段：透過本校職涯發展與實習/志工平台辦理線上問卷調查（109年6-7月辦理），學務處職涯中心將以信件、簡訊通知線上填答，亦惠請系所以有效管道協助轉知相關訊息以增進填答率。

			（二）第二階段：針對未填寫線上問卷同學以電訪方式調查（109年8-10月辦理）。

			二、關於畢業生流向問卷，調查年度之畢業生登錄帳號為學號，登錄密碼為身份證字號前六碼（含大寫英文及前五位數字），約三分鐘即可完成作答，非屬調查年度之畢業生將無法登錄；若完成填答者，本年度電訪員將不再撥打電話調查，預期將有效撙節受訪者寶貴時間並避免打擾作息。

			三、查本校部分院系所通知畢業校友之方式，多透過「校友子系統—校友資料維護查詢功能」寄發通知信件或傳送簡訊通知，本中心已委請電算中心針對該系統新增「月份」篩選功能，本次篩選調查範圍如次：

			（一）107學年度：請篩選107年8月至108年7月之畢業生資料。

			（二）105學年度：請篩選105年8月至106年7月之畢業生資料。

			（三）103學年度：請篩選103年8月至104年7月之畢業生資料。

			四、調查結果配合校務資訊公開政策，將援例於次年3月公布於本校校務資訊公開專區提供查閱及下載（路徑為：本校首頁/校務暨財務公開專區/學校績效表現/畢業生流向現況），106-108學年度畢業生流向調查結果業已公告，歡迎參閱。

			五、本校畢業生流向調查作業聯絡窗口：學務處職涯中心趙紀綱先生（分機：63257；E-MAIL：[cgchao@nccu.edu.tw](mailto:cgchao@nccu.edu.tw)）。

一、​本校自108學年度第1學期起，擴大輔系專班課程修課學生免收修課學分費，然爲營造校內永續經營之跨域學習環境，自113學年度第1學期起本校學生修習擴大輔系專班課程(科目代號前3碼為010)恢復收取學分費。

二、​自113學年度第1學期起學生取得擴大輔系資格者，修習擴大輔系課程(科目代號前3碼為010)收取百分之80學分費，112學年度(含)前具擴大輔系身分學生修習該專班課程維持免繳學分費。

三、原「國立政治大學擴大辦理輔系處理準則」於108學年度第1學期因說明一理由暫停適用，自即刻起恢復適用。

四、本案有關資訊公開、研議公開過程資訊，及相關收費細節請參閱教務處網站學雜費專區之其他項下，[112學年度第2學期校內推動擴大輔系恢復收費方案歷程專頁](https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/zh//index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=5291)。

問卷調查日文系的小班課程(日語會話演習、日文習作)是否上下學期換班? 結果不同意換班與同意換班差距不大，且票數非常地接近。

 

就細項來看，大一生與雙主修生是不同意換班較多，大二以上則是同意換班較多。依此結果經112學年度第2學期第二次系務會議之決議

 

113學年度開始日語會話演習(一)、日文習作(一) 不換班，日語會話演習(二)、日文習作(二)上下學期換班。

各位同學好

大家還記得職涯講座以及商務日語課程演講的湯庭瑜學姊嗎? 

遠距上課期間，湯庭瑜學姊特別為即將畢業的大四學弟妹，提供線上履歷健檢服務活動。

歡迎有興趣的應屆畢業生(碩士班亦可)報名。

一、活動名稱：【新卒限定！線上履歷健檢】

二、流程：

（1）活動期間：6/7～6/30

（2）同學們將寫好的履歷寄至 hychiao@nccu.edu.tw 喬老師收  (由喬老師先進行統一收件)。

  (3)  寄給喬老師的電郵，請寫上主旨和寄件人。範例如下:

　　 主旨統一:報名保聖那線上履歷健檢 （系所年級 中文全名）

　　 例:報名保聖那線上履歷健檢 （日文四 王小明）

　　 喬老師提醒大家，請於寄件後填寫表單登錄https://forms.gle/U2YnF5QDSYd9T1CY6

（4）湯學姊將進行後續指導（以Email或電話聯繫為主）

三、留意事項

（1）限大四、碩班等應屆畢業生

（2）【必須】提供中、日文履歷兩種版本

（3）格式不拘，亦可使用保聖那的格式（點擊下列連結下載）

[Pasona中文履歷制訂格式](https://register.pasona.com.tw/pdata/PasonaResume/PasonaResumeForm_CH.docx)

[Pasona日文履歷制訂格式](https://register.pasona.com.tw/pdata/PasonaResume/PasonaResumeForm_JP.docx)

（4）履歷檔名必須包含校名、系名及中文全名（例如：保聖那大學日文系保小那中文履歷）

（5）履歷中必須載明姓名、聯絡方式（電話、email），以供後續個別聯繫指導

【2】第6回アジア未来会議　論文募集のお知らせ

 

新型コロナウイルスによるパンデミックによって、これから世界が大きく変わるでしょうが、問題はどのように変わるか今はわからないことです。第6回アジア未来会議はまだ１年以上先のことですから、できるだけ台湾の状況と台湾への旅行情報を参加者の皆さんと共有しながら準備を進めてまいります。最悪の場合には、関係者の安全のため延期等もありえます。しかしながら、状況が落ち着き、私たちが一堂に会することができれば、この会議はポストコロナのアジアと世界を語り合う絶好の場となるでしょう。１日も早く全世界で新型コロナウイルスが収束することを祈りつつ、アジア未来会議の開催に対する皆さまのご理解とご協力、そしてご参加をお願いいたします。

 

◆第6回アジア未来会議

「アジアを創る、未来へ繋ぐ－みんなの問題、みんなで解決」

 

会期：2021年8月27日（金）～31日（火）（到着日、出発日を含む）

会場：中国文化大学（台北市）発表要旨の投稿締切：

・奨学金、優秀賞に応募する場合　 2020年8月31日（月）

・奨学金、優秀賞に応募しない場合　2021年2月28日（日）

 

募集要項は下記リンクをご覧ください。

画面上のタブで言語（英語、日本語、中国語）を選んでください。

[http://www.aisf.or.jp/AFC/2021/call-for-papers/](http://www.aisf.or.jp/AFC/2021/call-for-papers/)

 

アジア未来会議は、日本で学んだ人や日本に関心のある人が集い、アジアの未来について語る＜場＞を提供します。アジア未来会議は、学際性を核としており、グローバル化に伴う様々な課題を、科学技術の開発や経営分析だけでなく、環境、政治、教育、芸術、文化の課題も視野にいれた多面的な取り組みを奨励します。皆様のご参加をお待ちしています。

[海報宣傳](https://japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/upload/6/doc/29455/海報設計-1(含說明文字).png)

演講題目：琉球をめぐる十九世紀国際関係史

琉球王國，十七世紀起成為薩摩藩支配的附庸國，處於日中兩屬狀態。十九世紀後期琉球成為日本的「沖繩」，並在二戰後被美國軍事占領近三十年，其獨特的歷史背景以及地理上的區隔，讓現今的沖縄在日本有著極為特殊的地位。

本演講將一揭沖縄神秘的歷史面紗，探討琉球於十九世紀時是如何成為日、清、歐美列強三方政治外交角力的場域，並分析當時琉球與不同勢力簽訂之條約內容與相關史料，進一步去思考琉球對於現今的日本具有何種意義。

講者：山城智史(名櫻大學國際學部 國際文化學科 上級准教授)

[poster](https://japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/upload/6/doc/30900/源氏物語翻譯經驗談.jpg)

【講座緣起】

國立政治大學翻譯與跨文化研究中心自2023年8月起，在外語學院與高教深耕計畫的支持下，將舉辦多場翻譯系列講座與教育活動，其中「翻譯大師講座」每學期將舉辦兩場，邀請台灣國內知名翻譯學者與研究者，分享其學思歷程。

113學年度第一學期的第二場翻譯大師講座邀請林水福老師蒞校演講。林水福老師畢業於日本國立東北大學，是國內研究日本文學名著《源氏物語》的第一人 ，也大量譯介遠藤周作和谷崎潤一郎等日本近現代文學大家之作。今年林水福老師翻譯《源氏物語》出版，該書耗時近4年，總字數達90萬字，是繼林文月譯本之後，睽違46年的全新譯本。本次演講林水福老師將無私分享從事《源氏物語》翻譯的點滴，歡迎踴躍報名，實體與線上同步舉行。

【講者簡介】

1953年生於雲林縣二崙鄉打牛湳村。輔仁大學東方語文學系畢。日本國立東北大學碩士及文學博士學位。

曾任臺北駐日經濟文化代表處臺北文化中心首任主任、國立高雄第一科技大學副校長、外語學院院長、輔仁大學外語學院院長、日本國立東北大學客座研究員、日本梅光女學院大學副教授、中國青年寫作協會理事長、台灣日語教育學會理事長、台灣文學協會理事長、台灣石川啄木學會會長、台灣芥川龍之介學會會長。

著有《解讀源氏物語》《日本文學導遊》、《源氏物語的女性》等約十冊；翻譯遠藤周作、谷崎潤一郎、川端康成、種田山頭火等的作品約六十冊。獲五四獎文學活動獎、南投縣玉山文學貢獻獎。

【主持人】

林侑毅 (政大韓文系助理教授、翻譯與跨文化研究中心主任)

日期：2021-03-25

[海報](https://japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/upload/6/doc/10068/166404837_443017540256330_4074419858320215475_n.png)

講題：「鬼的文化史與《鬼滅之刃》的世界」

 

演講連結：[https://ctld.video.nccu.edu.tw/km/1462](https://ctld.video.nccu.edu.tw/km/1462)

 

內容摘要：

    當漢字傳入日本時，日本人為何選擇「鬼」這個字來呈現「oni」的概念？古文獻中記錄「鬼吃人」（出雲國風土記）及「穢悪疫鬼」（延喜式），而這二個本質，也與《鬼滅之刃》中對「鬼」的設定有相通之處。本演講將以《鬼滅之刃》為中心，來看鬼的愛與仇，以及本作品給予當代的訊息及反思。

 

講者資料

講者：沈美雪 (中國文化大學日本語文學系副教授)

專長：俳文學、次文化研究

次文化研究之相關經歷：宅歷40年的資深動漫宅、日本漫畫學會會員。「第六屆御宅文化學術研討會暨巴哈姆特論文獎」主辦人、翻譯過漫畫百餘本。在文化大學開設「日本動漫與次文化」「跨域人文：日本動漫御宅學」等課程。協助國內大專教育次文化相關研討會、研習營之舉辦，擔任評論者或專題演講等。關於次文化研究除相關學術論文外，亦有專文「跨越時空 不變的愛－談《跳躍吧！時空少女》與《你的名字。》」（聯合文學422期）」，及監修《湯本豪一：今昔妖怪大鑑》《湯本豪一 古今妖怪纍纍》（中文版監修、三采文化）、《台湾における日本人声優ブームの受容と現在》（楊雅婷著、致良文化）等書。

日期：2021-01-13

本系所開設之選修課程「日文現代文學賞析2」(科目代號：556787-001)、「中日語言研究演習1」(科目代號：556825-001)、「日本古典文法」(科目代號：556901-001)為學碩合開之課程，歡迎有興趣的大三/大四生皆可選修。

109學年度的「日語會話演習(一)」、「日語會話演習(二)」、「日文習作(一)」、「日文習作(二)」開設為A/B/C三班。一班人數上限25人。109學年度第2學期由系統進行換班(即更換任課老師)。為求三班人數、程度均等，日文系的同學(包含雙主修)若無特殊身心狀況並經系所同意，都不得退選換班。

如同學遇下學期衝堂問題，不修習「日語會話演習(一)」、「日語會話演習(二)」、「日文習作(一)」、「日文習作(二)」等課程，可填寫附件的退課申請書(如附件)，於2月2日前(二)送來系辦代為辦理。但2月3日(三)後，請同學自行於加簽暨退課期間至註冊組辦理。

(再提醒)因應107學年度入學之同學無需修習「日語會話演習(三)」，故109學年度本系無開設「日語會話演習(三)」，若未修習過的同學可以選修「商務日語1/2」、「日譯中理論與實務1/2」「日語主題討論與簡報訓練1/2」的學分來抵免。

日期：2020-05-29

依據：

「國立政治大學學生選課辦法」。

公告事項：

一、109學年度第1學期各項選課事宜依旨揭日程表辦理。

二、本校選課應於網路選課系統進行，期程簡要說明如下：

（一）公告開課課程及選課訊息：7月14日起。

（二）開放追蹤清單登記：8月4日起。

（三）「學士班學生超減修習學分數」申請：

第一階段：8月4日至8月17日申請，8月18日至8月19日學系審核。

第二階段：8月20日至9月7日申請，9月8日至9月9日學系審核。

（四）「學士班四年級學生體育補修」申請：8月4日至9月7日。

（五）「被擋修科目允許選課登記」申請：8月18日至9月21日下午5時止。

（六）第一階段初選登記：8月24日上午9時至8月26日下午5時止。

（七）第二階段初選登記：8月31日上午9時至9月2日下午5時止。

（八）加退選登記及分發：9月14日上午9時至9月21日下午5時止。

（九）加簽暨退課單列印及申請：9月22日上午9時至9月29日，自103學年度起，退課不計額度；學士班學生加簽課程以5門課為限；碩、博士班加簽課程以3門課為限，選課學分總數仍依學分上下限規定。

（十）非歸責學生事由選課處理：10月5日至10月12日下午5時止。

（十一）已選上課程「允許擋修及重複修習」申請：8月24日至10月12日下午5時止。

（十二）網路確認選課結果：10月6日至10月13日。

（十三）棄修單列印及申請：列印時間為11月2日上午9時至11月27日下午5時止，收件時間為11月16日至11月27日下午5時止。

三、第一階段初選未選上的課程，學生應於初選第二階段重新登記；第二階段初選分發未選上科目進入遞補清單，待加退選期間進行遞補，各階段分發上限為學生修習學分上限。

四、學生若因系統分發錯誤等非歸責學生之事由，得於規定期間內附報告書及證明文件，依程序送請教務長同意後辦理選課。

五、本校或外校學生辦理「國內校際選課申請作業」，施行線上申請。「國內校際選課申請系統」連結置於本校選課系統。申請程序為，登入該系統、輸入資料、登記選課並列印申請表單，經相關單位審核同意、繳納學分費後，送註冊組登錄選課資料。

六、為發送選課結果，請同學事先確認電子郵件帳號之正確性，並於規定期間內透過網路或電子郵件信箱查詢選課結果，亦可於選課期間透過選課系統之「課表」頁籤，取得即時的課表。

七、選課日程表及選課相關訊息另公告於教務處網站/註冊組/選課訊息。

日期：2020-06-24

 

2020暑期國際課程── 「文化探索・服務創新：博物館文物典藏與應用」招生中！

日文系主要參與「課程一：漢字文化圈的探索」之開課，上課以華語和日語為主，介紹台灣故宮博物院的文物。此課程學分認定為109學年度上學期兩學分。課程之特色如下，課程大綱詳細介紹如附檔。報名期限至7/5截止，請同學們把握機會。

 

課程特色:

「文化探索・服務創新：博物館文物典藏與應用」計畫是以橫跨各知識領域，結合本校文學、外語學院、商學院教師，並邀請國立故宮博物院研究員，日本長崎大學多文化社會學步、早稻田大學教授等師資共同策劃之國際課程。本課程以國立故宮博物院為研究學習之場域，期待臺、日及其他國家學生共同組成合作學習，透過國立故宮博物院或台灣重要博物館典藏的具體文物，理解歷史、鑑賞藝術，進而展開探索。在探索的道路中上，以多媒體互動，或文創設計等角度，試著轉譯文物自身的訊息、文物創作的意境，並以創新的材質及想法表現當代心靈與歷史文物之間的「對話」。

 

課程計畫分成以下兩種:

一、漢字文化圈的探索：博物館典藏文物的鑒賞及文化思索（華語+日語上課）：

[http://hidschool.nccu.edu.tw/2020/06/18/2020summer_courses_eccc/](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=http%3A%2F%2Fhidschool.nccu.edu.tw%2F2020%2F06%2F18%2F2020summer_courses_eccc%2F%3Ffbclid%3DIwAR2ca1iDNYOhikUSknr-b_PrFlUeb3fLpRsAfaZ0qFs153J-2FNeFirI8Oc&h=AT0exZzKUDWVh8AG5OB7YnpKxJw0LERHzSaJMWY2_SeN0W6D9i8QfNmBKp6yGEkQ3dTuGik1K6qm58kY8JGbShxBeD1CFQHo2-3hUjWaM6c5eW9KUdiy4rwlViqO6Cc6Mfuq&__tn__=-UK-R&c[0]=AT0rVkmA2sAmkby7HJl8WPmWBZINLV__5YnQ3iiCMcBIZtVy6yZS_BrhuegLTPj7IIjUMScuJUdkKQKaxZ-2gE-HI7dO-WWOy4qBMpbGdRiLL3Xs9ybirFS_00AdUcza3r2SvNh3KLQkXtvV_LQIu0oolSYdBjAOPeAckR0iU6sXNfp9dVaP8RssB2g0PnCTKqT3w4m8nEAk8k_iLWHzL9I787WtLg)

 

二、「知識櫥窗」的服務創新：國立故宮博物院的文創行銷（全英文上課）：

[http://hidschool.nccu.edu.tw/2020/06/19/2020summer_courses_npm/](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=http%3A%2F%2Fhidschool.nccu.edu.tw%2F2020%2F06%2F19%2F2020summer_courses_npm%2F%3Ffbclid%3DIwAR3YsbdgRTRwB_B0ICY7XWNw80w8DCuliST9HUFRkEgzlqZa7EvFqZ1-bcU&h=AT19vC5GDuuZd1FCF37A7v9KiUR_AvYS5fzqjuptcYDRqFoVn-7nYIR04852H3uLyqtCL8EUyV8fjFDeoPnPlVp8g6XEf7m-TaoWVECUDTEeieoapOk87XUiy88UAKvCKnVv&__tn__=-UK-R&c[0]=AT0rVkmA2sAmkby7HJl8WPmWBZINLV__5YnQ3iiCMcBIZtVy6yZS_BrhuegLTPj7IIjUMScuJUdkKQKaxZ-2gE-HI7dO-WWOy4qBMpbGdRiLL3Xs9ybirFS_00AdUcza3r2SvNh3KLQkXtvV_LQIu0oolSYdBjAOPeAckR0iU6sXNfp9dVaP8RssB2g0PnCTKqT3w4m8nEAk8k_iLWHzL9I787WtLg)

日期：2021-08-11

各位同學們好！

 

日文系與台史所即將於110學年度第1學期合開課程「台灣文化初探」，

將由日文系的葉秉杰老師、金想容老師以及台史所的前田直樹老師、周俊宇老師共同授課，主要對象為日籍學生以及台灣的日語學習者。

 

課程內容將從語言、社會文化、歷史等各個角度來介紹台灣，以期讓日籍學生有機會認識台灣文化，同時也讓台灣之日語學習者對自國文化進一步省思，並且培養用外語來介紹台灣文化的能力。此外，本課程也企圖藉由分組以及課堂活動等設計，期使日籍學生與台籍學生共同學習、達到雙向交流的目的，並且增進國際視野。

 

【課程基本資訊】

上課時間：四34

學分數：2學分

招收人數：日文系學士班15人  *台史所以及日籍生人數請見台史所及國合處公告

報名時間：8/31-9/6中午前(若額滿會先將選課登記表提前關閉)

選課登記網址：[https://forms.gle/tq8pSDAimLQqKDFJ7](https://forms.gle/tq8pSDAimLQqKDFJ7)

 

更多詳細內容請見課程大綱(可見附加檔)

超豪華教師陣容，豐富多彩的課程內容與交流機會，千萬不要錯過！

 

【備註】

1.本課程將不開放於選課系統選課，請欲選課的同學填寫選課登記表單，人數超過時將列備取名單，請再等候email通知結果。

2.語言程度：(1)非日籍生: 須具備日文檢定N2(含)以上能力 (2)非本籍生: 須具備能簡單溝通的中文能力。

日文系擴大輔系課程有幾點注意事項如下：

 

關於112學年以前(含112)申請輔系的同學：

請留意「日語讀本一」與「日語聽力練習」這兩門科目為113學年度起輔系生必修科目，112學年以前(含112)的輔系同學請選修「初級日語」與「日語演習一」。

「初級日語」與「日語演習一」的開課量會逐年遞減，114學年只剩一班，若今年沒有衝堂，請多多把握今年機會。

 

關於113學年申請輔系的同學：

由於「日語讀本一」與「日語聽力練習」已額滿，替代方案如下：

日語讀本一：大學外文（日文）、輔系初級日語可抵免，或以日文檢定跳修（請見日文系官網常見問題）

日語聽力練習：將於星期五78節加開一門日語聽力練習，請未選上的同學優先以這時段為考量，未免選課人數不足以開班。真的無法再請另外兩班老師加簽。日文系所有課程未開放加簽單列印，敬請至本系網站「資訊專區」→「下載專區」→「大學部」下載加簽單。（加簽單請於加簽暨退課階段再送至系辦，提早送不受理）

需留意輔系生若選本系選修課，隨班附讀也需收費，且是全額收費。詳見「113學年度擴大輔系恢復收費身分基準一覽表」。

 

 ＊已跟老師聯繫過加簽事宜的同學，記得通知老師是要加選新開課，還是繼續加簽。每位老師加簽原則不同，有的老師是優先讓延畢生加簽，有的老師有其他優先順序，系上尊重任課老師的原則。

日文系擴大輔系課程有幾點注意事項如下：

2025.9.1加退選階段開放全校學生選課。若課程已額滿，請同學自行評估遞補成功的可能性。

關於112學年以前(含112)申請輔系的同學：

請留意「日語讀本一」與「日語讀本二」為113學年度起輔系生必修科目，112學年以前(含112)的輔系同學請選修「初級日語」與「中級日語」。

 114學年的「初級日語」為最後一堂初級日語，請112學年以前(含112)的輔系同學把握今年最後機會。

115學年度「中級日語」只剩一班，請112學年以前(含112)的輔系同學，今年若沒衝堂的話，趕緊將中級日語選起來。

「日語演習一」請以「日語聽力練習」抵免，「日語演習二」請以「進階日語聽力練習」抵免，以一堂課抵一堂課，而不是以一堂2學分的課抵二堂1學分的課。

關於113學年起申請輔系的同學：

請優先加選尚未額滿之班級，協助課程順利開課。(滿20人開課)

若選日文系本系選修課，隨班附讀也需收費，且是全額收費。詳見「擴大輔系恢復收費身分基準一覽表」。

日文系所有課程未開放加簽單列印，敬請至本系網站「系所介紹」→「規章表格」→「學生相關」下載加簽單。（加簽單請於加簽暨退課階段再送至系辦，提早送不受理）

每位老師加簽原則不同，有的老師是優先讓延畢生加簽，有的老師有其他優先順序，系上尊重任課老師的原則。

日期：2025-07-07

【關於本系課程】

本系所開設之選修課程「日本古典文法」(科目代號：556901001) 為學碩合開之課程，歡迎有興趣的大三/大四生皆可選修。

本系所開之選修課程「東亞文化的共融與和平」雖為學碩合開之暑期密集課程，惟該課程之選課登記已於4月8日（二）截止，不再開放加選，敬請見諒。

114學年度「日語會話演習（一）」、「日語會話演習（二）」、「日文習作（一）」及「日文習作（二）」均開設A／B／C三班，每班人數上限為20人。如需加簽，亦以每班20人為限，恕無法超額。其中，114學年度第1學期的「日語會話演習（二）」、「日文習作（一）」之B班、「日文習作（二）」，將由系統進行自動換班（即更換任課教師）。為求三班人數、程度均等，日文系的同學(包含雙主修)若無特殊身心狀況並經系所同意，都不得退選換班。

若同學遇下學期衝堂問題，確定不修習「日語會話演習(二)」、「日文習作(一)」、「日文習作(二)」等課程，可填寫附件的退課申請書(如附件)，於8月28日前(四)送來系辦代為辦理。(可收電子檔，請寄至japanese@nccu.edu.tw)，但8月28日(四)以後，請同學自行於加簽暨退課期間至註冊組辦理。

【關於輔系課程】

自113學年度起，所有輔系課程需滿20人(含)才會開課，20人以下課程將視情況於加簽暨退課後停開。系辦確定停開後會通知任課老師。請同學要自行隨時觀察選課情形。

輔系課程的「日語讀本(一)」、「日語讀本(二)」為適用113學年度起(含113學年度)之輔系生，113學年度以前之輔系生請選修「初級日語」或「中級日語」。詳見[擴大輔系替代科目一覽表](https://japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=2330&id=4104)

114學年度初級日語為最後一班，115學年度將改制為「日語讀本(一)」。

「日語演習(一)」及「日語演習(二)」改制為「日語聽力練習」及「進階日語聽力練習」，113學年度以前輔系生請以日語聽力練習抵免日語演習一，進階日語聽力練習抵免日語演習二。

輔系課程相關疑問可再詳閱[常見問題](https://japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=2283&id=5854)。

【日本語文學系 微學程公告】

 

本系自114學年度起設置三個微學程，歡迎對日語學習、日本文化與社會、語言學理論與應用有興趣的同學踴躍修習！

 

微學程一覽

【基礎日語】微學程

【日語理論與應用】微學程

【認識日本】微學程

※須完成各微學程所規劃之課程，修達 12學分，方可申請取得該微學程認證。

※課程規劃及修課細則請參閱課程資訊→[微學程](https://japanese.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=13861&id=35035)。

※各微學程課程皆為隨班附讀。由於未設置微學程專屬身份，若需修習本系必修課程及群修課程，須以加簽方式選課，請留意下列事項：

·  「日語會話演習(一)」、「日文習作(一)」為小班授課，每班上限20人。若人數已滿，請於下一學期再行修習。

·  建議先修畢「初級日語」，再選修「日語語法」課程。

·  【基礎日語】微學程不適用本系之日語跳修辦法。

·  若課程人數已達上限，且任課教師加簽名額已滿，建議同學選修其他尚有餘額課程。

î若有疑問，歡迎聯絡日文系系辦：japanese@nccu.edu.tw

2、報到方式：以傳真方式辦理報到。錄取生於錄取名單公告後，須填妥「錄取生報到意願同意書」(如下方附件)傳真至本校教務處綜合業務組（02）29387495，並於上班時間來電確認，聯絡電話（02）2938-7892、2938-7893。逾時不予受理。

條件：

1.具助理教授（含）級以上教師資格或博士學位（錄取後驗正本，如為外國學歷，請於相關駐外館處辦妥驗證）。

2. 能夠教授日語基礎課程以及碩士班課程。並具備日語語言學相關學門專長之教師。

3.可擔任日文系相關課程、指導碩士論文，並具研究潛力。

4.能英語授課者尤佳。

 

※專任教師人員相關規定請參見本校人事室網站。

採通訊報名，第一階段資料審查後，將以電子郵件通知是否可以參加第二階段面試。

日期：2025-10-01

迪思科實習招募計劃

本系名額只有1名，但難得的實習機會，不但能學以致用，還能提升專業技能，為未來職涯奠定紮實基礎！有興趣的同學請填寫附件的日文履歷表，並請於 10 月 16 日(四)前寄至 japanese@nccu.edu.tw。

經書面審查後，我們將以E-MAIL通知入選同學與系主任面談的時間，面談結束後將通知最終甄選結果。

甄選上的同學DISCO會再面試，鼓勵同學踴躍報名，抓住這個寶貴的學習機會！

========================================================================================================

一，目的:

 

為培訓政治大學日本語文學系(以下簡稱: 政大日文系)在學學生的實務專才及增進實務技能，

迪思科高科技股份有限公司(以下簡稱: 迪思科)邀請政大日文系所推薦合適同學前往迪思科實習。

 

二，實習內容

 

實習期間：2026年1月12 至2026年3月27日

實習時間：實習期間每週可出勤24小時以上(可議)

實習地點：新北市新店區寶橋路188號9樓

實習部門：經營支援部

 

三，工作內容

 

中⇔日翻譯：公司內部文件、影片

公司企劃活動支援協辦

人事業務支援、辦公室總務支援等助理業務

企劃提案發想：公司內部改善提案、人事相關企劃

 

四，課程學習

 

半導體產業界介紹

企業文化活動

社會人禮儀、工作方法

作業發表 : 改善案實作後發表

 

五，薪資福利

 

時薪：200元

福利：雙月一次700元/人 聚餐補助

出差時高鐵、計程車、捷運等交通費全額支付

表現優異者有機會轉為正社員或是延長實習期間

 

六，招募條件

 

限大學在學生三年級以上

日文能力：日檢N2或具相等或以上能力

個性：積極主動、喜歡動腦思考、喜歡挑戰、細心、認真負責

 

七，期望學生藉由實習經驗可以提前接觸職場環境，不僅能夠提升翻譯能力、應變能力，對事物的察覺‧改善能力等皆會大幅提升。

也透過在迪思科實習可獲得半導體相關知識，拓展學習視野，並獲得事務上的實務經驗。

提醒：若未於 2025年8月26日參加說明會之同學，可參考以下連結了解完整實習內容與薪資福利。

 〈十六夜〉

總召：林珮瑢、廖品欣

單位：國立政治大學日本語文學系

================================

《歌舞伎町の女王》

編導：林珮瑢、張路嘉

翻譯：蔡浥平、劉又瑄、侯源富、鍾依耘

校對：陳璁、賴禾旻、林彥儒

翻譯/校對指導：王淑琴 老師

語言指導：吉田妙子 老師

================================

十六夜，意指農曆十五滿月後的夜晚，盈月必虧的首夜，象徵高峰後必迎來的衰亡。

1980年代，日本身處慾望無度的時代巔峰，人們揮霍所欲之物。新宿的歌舞伎町，正是泡沫經濟金玉其外的表象⋯⋯

面對十六夜的到來，如何在虛實中找回自己的初心？

================================

2024年 國立政治大學日本語文學系 日文之夜

 

〈真夜なか〉

 

總召：陳永信

副召：施少騫

單位：國立政治大學日本語文學系

 

—————————————————————

 

《銀河鉄道の夜》

 

導演：曾顯柔

編劇：霜村萌果、曾顯柔

原作：宮澤賢治

翻譯／校對：葉于嫺、張登凱、闕嘉盈

翻譯／校對指導：王淑琴 老師

語言指導：黑崎貴史 老師、吉田妙子 老師

 

—————————————————————

 

真夜なか，意指深夜之中。

而「真夜」的讀音「まよ」也同時寓意迷途。

 

在深夜之中，你會為繁星的璀璨奪目歌頌，還是跟隨月光踏著失落朦朧的舞步？

 

在深夜之中，又是誰迷失於此？

 

或許，藉由仰望夜空中的星宿，就可以在其中受到牽引而找尋回家的路，不再猶豫地尋覓真正的幸福。

 

—————————————————————

schedule

日本航空公司與日華青少年協會攜日本各大學之大學生來台至政大進行參訪，與本系學生相互交流，以促進台灣和日本兩國青年之交流及相互了解。

時間：3月5日（四）14:00～18:10

地點：季陶340108教室

報名資格：日文系本系、雙主修皆可參加。

建議程度：活動全程以日文進行，建議日文能力N2以上，能以日文表達自己想法者。

報名名額：10-25人(若超過會甄選)。

活動詳情：當天會將同學分組，請同學帶領日本同學參觀山上校區，並與日本同學以日文進行議題討論並發表，題目是ｲﾝﾀｰﾈｯﾄのｼｮｰﾄ動画の是非について，請同學事先查找資料、並進行簡單準備。詳細時程請參見報名表的時程。

山上校區舉例：道藩樓、季陶樓、百年樓、藝文中心、國際大樓、水岸電梯、蔣公銅像等。(可先查如何用日文介紹)

title: law57A.pdf
text:
國 立 政 治 大 學 外 語 課 程 限 修 辦 法
94.12.07外語學院第77次院務會議通過
95.03.27經94學年第二學期第一次教務會議通過
98.06.08經97學年第2學期第2次教務會議通過
第一條 國立政治大學(以下簡稱本校)為確保外語課程教學之公平
性，特訂定本辦法。
第二條 本校僑生及國際學生不得選修與其僑居地或國籍之官方語言
或主要使用語言相同之學士班語文課程。
第三條 一般生曾於外國中等學校以上就讀超過兩年以上者，亦不得
選修學士班該國語言之基礎外語課程，但經任課教師同意，
得修習進階課程。
第四條 凡應被限修卻自行修課者，該課程學分及成績不予承認。
第五條 本辦法經教務會議核定後實施，修訂時亦同。

title: 附件二國立政治大學學士班學生轉系規則.pdf
text:
國立政治大學學士班學生轉系規則
民國66年3月9日第420次行政會議通過
民國85年2月28日第537次行政會議修正
民國91年10月9日第579次行政會議修正通過第1、7、8條條文
民國92年12月10日第587次行政會議修正通過第1條條文
民國97年12月3日第617次行政會議修正通過第7條條文
民國103年12月31日第656次行政會議修正通過第3、4、5、6、7、8、9條條文
民國105年12月19日105學年度第1學期第2次教務會議修正通過第3條條文
民國105年12月28日政教校字第1050038284號函發布
民國109年2月17日108學年度第2學期臨時教務會議修正通過第1、4、5、6、7、9條條文
教育部109年6月17日臺教高(二)字第1090075903號函同意備查第1、4、5、6、7、9條條文
民國109年7月9日政教字第1090017838號函發布
民國113年6月3日112學年度第2學期第2次教務會議修正通過第9條、新增第10條條文
民國113年7月8日政教字第1130021899號函發布
第一條 本規則依據大學法及本校學則訂定之。
第二條 本校各學系修讀學士學位學生轉系悉依本規則辦理。
第三條 各學系錄取轉系學生名額，以不超過該學系當學年度一年級
原核定及分發新生名額之二成為原則。
大陸地區學生招生委員會分發之陸生得申請轉入 學系
（組），限於該學系（組）於學生轉入學年度教育部核定有
陸生錄取名額者。
第四條 轉入申請標準由學系自定之，並送教務處彙總公告。各學系
得以學業成績、其他優良表現等訂定標準或不限定申請資
格。
第五條 學生自一年級下學期起得申請轉系，學生轉入學系之年級由
轉入學系審核之。
降級轉系者，其應修學分數及必修科目，應依轉入年級學生
入學學年度必修科目表規定辦理。學生修業年限以轉入學系
之年級重新起算。
轉系以一次為限，學生申請轉系至多得申請兩個學系，由學
系審核轉系結果。同系轉組者，比照轉系各項規定辦理。
第六條 下列學生如確因分發不合志趣或其他因素無法在修讀學系
繼續肄業者，經校內輔導單位查實，修讀學系及轉入學系主
任同意後，得從寬核准：
一、國際學生。
二、僑生。
三、港澳生。
四、經身心障礙學生升學大專校院甄試委員會分發或領有身
心障礙手冊之學生。
1

第七條 轉系應於規定期間填妥學生轉系（組）申請表，未成年學生
須經法定代理人或監護人同意後，始得送交申請表。經修讀
學系同意，再向擬轉入學系申請，轉入學系主任同意錄取
後，由教務處依學生申請選填志願序核定各學系錄取名單，
簽請校長核定公告。
轉系經公告者，不得申請變更或撤銷。學生於申請轉系當學
期辦理休學者，取消其轉系核准資格。
第八條 各學系修讀學士學位轉學生及九十九學年度以前入學之推
薦甄選生不得申請轉系，但情況特殊提經教務會議通過者不
在此限。
離島外加名額學生不得申請轉系，並依離島地區學生保送高
級中等以上學校辦法規定辦理。
第九條 教學單位增設調整後轉系作業依下列規定辦理:
一、原教學單位整併、停招後，增設或新設教學單位專業領
域相近者，經與在籍學生溝通，以書面或會議形式取得
共識，得向新設教學單位申請所有在籍學生轉系，經該
單位同意及校長核定後，學生轉至相銜接之年級肄業。
二、教學單位增設學籍分組者，得依前款規定，專案簽請校
長核定原不分組所有在籍學生轉系(組)至學籍分組相銜
接之年級肄業。
三、本條轉系(組)作業申請，應在新設教學單位或增設學籍
分組經教育部核定成立學年期之前一學期完成。
原教學單位依前項程序完成在籍學生轉系(組)作業後，原修
讀該單位雙主修、輔系之學生，其雙主修、輔系修讀學籍併
同調整。
第一項轉系作業不受本規則第三條第一項轉系名額限制，且
本次轉系不計為第五條第三項轉系一次之次數。
第十條 本規則經教務會議通過後發布施行，修正時亦同。
2

| 外 交 學 系 | 一、申請登記資格： 1、一年級在原修業學系一年級上學期學業成績總平均七十五分以上。 2、二年級以上（含二年級）欲轉入本系者須前各學期學業成績總平均七十五分以上（如該學期出國選課 則免計），且至少修習本系認可之本校開設國際關係相關科目一門以上，且平均成績達八十分以上者。 二、 應繳文件： 1、 轉系申請表 2、 歷年成績單正本 3、 班級排名表正本 4、 一千字以內之書面說明，略述轉系動機及未來發展方向。（請以A4尺寸、標楷體、字型大小13，第 一頁右上角註明學號、系級、姓名）。請繳交紙本並同時寄送電子檔至外交系指定信箱 （dip50916@nccu.edu.tw） 5、 其他優異表現（右上角均須註明學號、系級、姓名）。 三、轉系考試： (請見下頁) 1、筆試科目：國際現勢(中英文筆試)。 筆試時間：114年3月21日(五)，詳細時間地點將於本系網頁公告。 2、面試： 面試時間：114年3月24日(一)，詳細時間地點將於本系網頁公告。 |
| 教 育 學 系 | 一、申請登記資格： 在原修業學系最後學年度上學期學業成績總平均 75 分以上，或曾修習本系教師所開專業科目 至少一門平均 80 分以上，操行成績 A 以上。 二、繳交文件: 1、中文在校歷年成績單正本及學生操行成績證明書，學生操行成績證明書請依總則說明第五 點申請。 2、申請轉入本系之動機與期望之書面報告（500 字左右）及其他有利於申請轉系之相關資料(如 英語檢定證明)。 三、轉系考試： 1、與本系審核委員面試。 2、轉系面試時間:至遲將於轉系申請開始前於本系網頁公告。 四、附註：轉系生非師資生。 |

What about being a student at ICI most excites you? |

【有勞健保】有

欲應徵的同學請來信部門招募助理 Jill (Jill@pasona.com.tw)

【工作地點】台北市大安區敦化南路二段65號6樓（近捷運信義安和站）

【工作設備】 有提供桌上型電腦

【工作內容】

1. 支援人事助理相關工作

2. 協助電話聯繫、文書處理、資料key-in 

3. 協助人事行銷活動

【其他備註】

保聖那是日本上市企業Pasona Group之臺灣子公司，已成立30多年，提供企業全方面人力資源服務，歡迎願意在畢業前累積日商實習經驗的同學應徵唷！

台北文化創意協會是Infinity Japan 日本無極限 當代藝術博覽會的主辦單位。

Infinity Japan自成立以來專注於引進當代藝術交流，今年即將邁入第十個年頭，也是疫情減緩後Infinity Japan的首場藝博會。每年邀請日本各行政區的藝廊來台展出，希望能夠帶給台灣最完整的日本當代藝術，並透過引進國際高知名度作品，與台灣當代視覺藝術領域深入交流。

今年將於8/4-6 在台北老爺酒店舉辦【Infinity Japan 2023日本無極限 當代藝術博覽會】，這次的志工招募活動，服務期滿且表現良好者，臺北文化創意協會將發給專屬時數證明。

現誠摯招募志工參與活動，我們歡迎喜愛日本藝術或想要近距離接觸藝術展會的同學們加入志工行列！有英文溝通能力,諳日文者佳。

志工時程：8/3-7(含佈展及撤展),另有活動時間依表格所示

地點：台北老爺酒店

工作內容：協助佈展與卸展，現場實際觀摩參與展覽場規劃、佈置、活動場控等、觀眾服務、前後台工作與管理等實務性工作

教育訓練：藝文導覽訓練

We're looking for an Associate, Business Development (Japanese Speaking)

仕事内容 - Klookの急成長するグローバルな顧客基盤のために、アトラクション、ツアー、交通、アクティビティ等の高品質なポートフォリオの開発と維持をサポート - アカウント管理： マーチャント（主にエクスペリエンスとモビリティのロングテールマーチャント）と連絡を取り、商品情報をアップデート。また予約・キャンセルの管理、カスタマーサービス関連への対応 - 商品の価格、在庫、コンテンツなどの面で、常に商品の品質を管理し、市場をリードするポジションを維持 - コーディネーション：社内の様々なチーム（日本オフィスとグローバルオフィスの両方）と密接に連携し、サプライヤーの効率化、カスタマーサービス満足度及びリピート率向上、スムーズな決済、テストブッキングとAPI接続の確認等を推進。柔軟な姿勢と細部への配慮は、当社のような速いペースで進む環境においては不可欠な要素です。 - アカウントサポート ：サプライヤーに対して、当社のプロセスやツールに関するトレーニングや日々の業務サポートを提供

 

対象となる方 - 3年以上の実務経験（アトラクション、アクティビティ、ツアー、交通機関などの旅行商品に関する経験があれば尚可 - 高いビジネスセンスと分析力、文章力、コミュニケーション能力 - 日本語が堪能であること(日本企業とのやり取りが可能であること) - 英語でのメール、読み書きができること(必須) - 自信にあふれ、自発的で目標達成志向のある方 - グローバルな視野を持ち、異なるバックグラウンドを持つ人々と仕事をすることに抵抗がない方 - 起業家精神に溢れ、協調性があり、自主的に行動できる方 - 戦略とビジネスへの影響度に基づいて仕事の優先順位付けができる方

 

Please apply via the link. Thank you!

Date 2022-06-17

工作名稱：

日商客服中心正職人員、日商客服中心實習人員

 

公司名稱：

ベルシステム24ホールディングス（日商鈴華股份有限公司、Bellsystem24 Holdings）

 

公司介紹：

本社位於東京都港區，東證一部上場企業，日本最大級客服中心，日本國內員工約20000名，2020年於台灣開設分公司，由本社100%出資成立。目前員工約80人左右。歡迎對於溝通技巧有自信的同學，或者想加入日商，體驗日商氛圍的同學前來應徵。

 

公司網站：[https://www.bell24.co.jp/ja/](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.bell24.co.jp%2Fja%2F%3Ffbclid%3DIwAR15oQigL4LYz8UHvDG6ywWyXUrOzfZGV4HhE8PYiS9gkP_yXoahEwbaYHo&h=AT34cZqwYkA21ymdMwqyctE_UeVw0n3azowFmbSp4E6jFp0fw4hzCFYCfvKhvEu4zN6k9FYi8Ieb6Nyw_H62fzk30g2VONHxv9cQeRpjcikzQNI37xJ5uPT17DsDry6ZmVM4&__tn__=-UK-R&c%5b0%5d=AT00ssMKQG7wHsAcs3k_qgmxgtlEmyyeppRF1RKf-h1xZ4SqQm8Bu-7FKOrKPhSy6e8CaF_Aka6T8pBfLOaMUdlBkm_2F1epwmhtMuDMG9yNGUeYFI6gIl2rLIK6xA0jDVYpFGEfqLGYHknkjZ07g4bzlCL1eCJyxHw)

 

薪資計算：

計時人員—研修期間約2-3週，時薪為170元，最少需要一週配合三天，一天八小時。研修結束後時薪調整為190元。整體優於一般打工實習業界。（含勞健保、六日也可輪班。）

全職人員—研修期間約2-3週，含基本薪資、全勤獎金、午餐費、績效獎金等，薪資約為33000-34000不等。（含勞健保）

 

要求條件：

①對於電話業務較沒有抵抗感

②對於學習新東西不排斥

③會基本電腦操作

☆有日語能力加分（程度不問）！

 

工作時間及樣態：

為排班制，目前最晚時間到21:00，主要為保健食品客服業務，如下訂、發貨、解決客戶困難等。配合的時間可再行討論。

每月有一次環境改善會議，例如想增加冰箱，想在廁所放酒精噴霧器，想購置硬體設備都可以提出。同時每三個月會有一次定例改善會議，可以針對非硬體提出建議，例如說想要生日假等。工作內容單純，上下班打卡制，基本上不會有加班的情況。

工作地點：新北市板橋區民族路168號（中華電信學院板橋所※近板橋捷運站）

104履歷投遞連結：[https://www.104.com.tw/company/1a2x6bl7b3](https://www.104.com.tw/company/1a2x6bl7b3)

投遞時表示經由政大日文系官網投遞，穩定工作三個月，且出勤達到90%以上您可得到一點業務獎金，歡迎同學前來投遞。

Date 2021-12-14

國立政治大學日本語文學系助理教授（含）級以上專任教師徵才公告

壹、條件：

具助理教授（含）級以上教師資格或博士學位（錄取後驗正本，如為外國學歷，請於相關駐外館處辦妥驗證）。

能夠教授日語基礎課程以及碩士班課程。具備日本語學．日語教育或日本近現代文學專長，並能指導日本語學．日語教育或日本近現代文學相關領域之碩士論文，以及有相關領域之研究著作。

外籍人士者則具可協助校務之中文溝通能力者為佳。

 

※專任教師人員相關規定請參見本校人事室網站。

※起聘日：預計111年8月1日

 

貳、應徵文件與方式：

意者請於111年1月4日（二）下午17:00前將下述文件以郵寄送達（非以郵戳為憑）─

1.履歷表

2.自傳

3.學歷證書影本

4.助理教授（含）級以上證書影本（若有）

5.中文或其他語言能力證明(若有)

6.其他各種資格證明（若有）

7.主要研究業績一覽(含博士論文)

8.主要論文(至多三件)

 

郵寄地址：

『11605台北市文山區指南路二段64號　政治大學日文系收』信封上請註明「應徵專任教師」

*以上各項應徵文件恕不退件，敬請預留備份。

 

參、面試試教：

 

第二階段面試：[暫訂於111年1月17日(一)進行，請預留時間]

1.研究發表20分鐘(口頭發表15分鐘+提問5分鐘)

2.試教高級日語20分鐘(口頭發表15分鐘+提問5分鐘)，以本系大三生為對象(日文程度約為日檢N2-N1)，內容自訂。

 

肆、聯絡通知：

採通訊通知，第一階段資料審查後，將以電子郵件通知是否可以參加第二階段面試。海外者視情況可用線上面試。

聯絡人：陳小姐（japanese@nccu.edu.tw），電話：02-29393091（分機）62167

希望能廣納貴校「精通日文且想培養行銷技能」的人才，

 

希望協助發佈的職缺資訊如下：

＊職缺說明：行銷助理

＊職務性質：兼職

			＊職務說明：

◉我們正在找行銷團隊的新成員◉

			 想一窺遊戲業中各個專案是如何將不同遊戲推廣給玩家嗎？

			 想了解在日商公司中的行銷工作是如何運作嗎？

			 加入我們的團隊！你將能接觸到從遊戲市場調查，到品牌、社群、廣告、公關等多元面向的行銷工作。

			實際運用您的日文能力，負責翻譯行銷相關文件，

			歡迎「精通日文且想培養行銷技能」的學生！

			 【工作内容】

			• 行政文書處理

			• 中日文件翻譯

			• 內外部溝通協調

			• 與團隊共同執行市場調查、品牌、社群、廣告、公關等事務

			• 其他主管交辦事項

			＊技能條件

◼︎ 必備條件

			• 具有日文 N2 以上的能力（讀＆寫精通）

			• 中 ⇌ 日文翻譯能力

			• 熟悉各類文書軟體（Word、Excel 函數、PPT、Mac系統）及雲端作業系統

			• 對數字有概念

			◼︎ 加分條件

			• 具有英文讀寫中等能力，可使用文字基礎應對

			• 喜歡接觸與遊玩各類手機遊戲

			◼︎ 人格特質

			• 細心負責

			• 溝通組織能力

			• 擁有學習熱情，能與團隊共同成長

＊排班資訊

			希望能配合半年，一週需出勤三天

			除週三必須排班之外，其他天的時數可再討論！

			公司上班時間為週一到週五 09:00-18:00（中間休息一個小時）

＊工作地點

			台北市中正區羅斯福路二段100號20F (距捷運古亭站50公尺)

			新人訓練期間需依規定進公司，後續若狀況穩定，可依情況提供遠端工作機會！

			＊查看更多資訊與投遞履歷請見 ：

日文翻譯工讀生

工作內容：

日文文件、教材翻譯

補習班各項事務手續

現場來客接待、電話對應

補習班來客、學員對應

公司服務介紹

環境維護

主管交辦事項

 

工作時間：

1.　每週排班 2~4 日

2.　排班 - 平日 16:30 ~ 21:30 / 假日 11:00~17:00 為主，每日 2 小時以上，視每月需求調整時段與時數

3.　需可配合半年以上

 

工作性質： 兼職-長期工讀

未來前景：

工作中需運用日語，適合日商就職希望者

完整紮實的教育訓練，適合想運用打工機會增進個人能力者

3.　日商極重視的「相．連．報」訓練，提前接觸辦公室文化

4.　享 JPTIP 日語課程學習優惠

 

【JPTIP相關網站】

JPTIP總官網：https://www.jptip.com

JPTIP日語學校：https://school.jptip.com

JPTIP日本留學：https://www.jptip.com.tw

JPTIP日本就職：https://www.jptipjob.com

工作待遇：時薪 168元

條件要求：

1. 日檢程度 N2以上，N1尤佳

2. 日文聽說讀寫優

3. 極需細心，且需熟悉電腦文書作業(word、excel)

4. 正向、積極、有笑容，不害怕面對人

5. 請附詳細履歷 (面試時將同時進行日文筆試測驗)

 

福利制度：勞保/健保/團體保險

應徵方式：請履歷至 [hr@jptip.co.jp](mailto:hr@jptip.co.jp)

          或電洽 02-2331-0109#217方小姐

          104人力銀行:https://www.104.com.tw/company/cyae5w8?jobsource=cs_2018indexpoc

 

JPTIP以台日合作事業之諮詢顧問業起家，深知國際合作之成功及維繫有賴於優秀人才之永續培育經營。為了對新世代的「聯繫台灣及日本的人才培育事業」貢獻一份心力，2009年展開日本人才教育事業，現在已是台灣最大的日本留遊學．打工度假、日本人才工作介紹機構，同時也成為台灣學生人數最多的日語人才培訓機構。除了在日本東京、台灣以外，在2020年與越南和緬甸當地創立JPTIP當地子公司，從日語學習到日本留學、就職的一站式服務成功拓展進軍東南亞市場。

 

JPTIP的日本人才教育不只注重培養學員日本語的實際運用能力，更致力於培育通曉企業組織文化及商業禮儀的國際企業人才。期許為本公司顧問部門的客戶提供優質的國際企業人才，並藉此激勵自己努力提升人才教育水準。除了提供台灣，東南亞等學子從學習到從學習到日本留學、就職的一站式服務之外，相對的也幫忙日本的各式學校及企業在海外做招募、招生，行銷活動宣傳。

 

公司多元化的工作內容，讓您不僅能活用日語專長、更能多方面學習，進而自我成長，除了自我充實外，更能有效發揮所長，達成自己的人生目標！

～歡迎加入JPTIP，成為台日交流的橋樑～

Date 2022-04-08

國立政治大學日本語文學系助理教授（含）級以上專任約聘教師徵才公告

 

壹、條件：

具助理教授（含）級以上教師資格或博士學位（錄取後驗正本，如為外國學歷，請於相關駐外館處辦妥驗證）。

能夠教授日語基礎課程以及碩士班課程。具備日本語學．日語教育專長，並能指導日本語學．日語教育相關領域之碩士論文，以及有相關領域之研究著作。

外籍人士者則具可協助校務之中文溝通能力者為佳。

 

※專任教師人員相關規定請參見本校人事室網站。

※起聘日：預計111年8月1日

 

貳、應徵文件與方式：

意者請於111年5月2日（一）中午12:00前將下述文件以郵寄送達（非以郵戳為憑）─

 

履歷表

自傳

學歷證書影本

助理教授（含）級以上證書影本（若有）

中文或其他語言能力證明(若有)

其他各種資格證明（若有）

主要研究業績一覽(含博士論文)

主要論文(至多三件)

 

郵寄地址：

『11605台北市文山區指南路二段64號　政治大學日文系收』信封上請註明「應徵專任教師」

*以上各項應徵文件恕不退件，敬請預留備份。

 

參、面試試教：

 

第二階段面試：[暫訂於111年5月13日(五)進行，請預留時間]

1.研究發表20分鐘(口頭發表15分鐘+提問5分鐘)

2.試教高級日語20分鐘(口頭發表15分鐘+提問5分鐘)，以本系大三生為對象(日文程度約為日檢N2-N1)，內容自訂。

 

肆、聯絡通知：

採通訊通知，第一階段資料審查後，將以電子郵件通知是否可以參加第二階段面試。海外者視情況可用線上面試。

Date 2025-03-27

List of Graduate Student Scholarship Recipients：

[Graduate Student Scholarship – Applications Open Until 5/2]

Applications for the Graduate Student Scholarship for this semester are now open and will be accepted until Friday, May 2, 12:00 PM. Interested students should prepare all required documents and submit them to the Department of Japanese Office before the deadline. Thank you!

Based on the "NCCU College of Foreign Languages and Literature Guidelines for Graduate Student Scholarships."

Eligibility:

Master’s students (1st and 2nd year) and doctoral students (1st, 2nd, and 3rd year) enrolled in departments under the College of Foreign Languages and Literature.

Ineligible students: Part-time graduate students, trainee students, students on leave of absence, and exchange students.

Required Documents:

	(1) Application form (Download from the College of Foreign Languages and Literature website)

	(2) Academic transcript

	(3) Other supporting documents, such as:

Proof of participation in academic activities (e.g., presented papers or certificates of participation in academic conferences)

Date 2025-03-06

Application Period:

From now until April 30, 2025 (Wednesday) at 5:00 PM sharp (late applications will not be accepted)

Eligibility:

Currently enrolled junior or senior undergraduate students in the Department (excluding students who have extended their studies)

Must have an average academic and conduct grade of 80 or above in the 112 academic year

Students who have previously received the Satoru Nitori Scholarship from the department are not eligible

Must not be receiving government funding or any other scholarships during this academic year

Number of Awards: 2 recipients (selected based on academic merit)

Award Amount: NT$5,000 per recipient

Required Documents:

One completed application form (please download from the attachment)

One complete transcript (including conduct grades; students from low-income households may attach supporting documents)

One proof of not receiving public funding or other scholarships (stamp available at the Student Assistance Division)

Please prepare and submit all documents before the deadline.

Date 2022-06-30

This process is conducted according to the university’s 111th Academic Year Calendar and the “National Chengchi University Student Credit Transfer Regulations.”

To accommodate the schedule changes for the bachelor’s program placement test announcement, credit transfer applications for new students will be handled separately for graduate students (master’s and doctoral, including in-service programs) and bachelor’s students (including transfer students) starting this academic year. The application schedules are as follows:

(1) Graduate students (master’s, doctoral, including in-service programs) may apply from August 2, 2022 (Tuesday) to August 5, 2022 (Friday), between 9:00 AM–12:00 PM and 2:00 PM–4:00 PM daily.

(2) Bachelor’s new students (including transfer students) may apply from August 17, 2022 (Wednesday) to August 23, 2022 (Tuesday), between 9:00 AM–12:00 PM and 2:00 PM–4:00 PM daily.

Required documents for credit transfer application:

(1) Credit Transfer Application Form (please do not print double-sided to facilitate approval; form attached below).

(2) Original official transcript in Chinese from the previously graduated or attended school.

(3) For applications involving general education courses or as requested by the department, please provide the original course syllabus from the previous institution. (This is mandatory!)

(4) Course Recognition Form for Graduate Programs: If you have earned a degree from a previous program and want to apply for credit transfer based on passed courses from that stage, please fill out this form and obtain approval from the authorized office of the previous school.

Applications for the “Short-term Study Abroad Subsidy to Encourage Students to Study Abroad” for the 1st semester of the 113 academic year are now open and will be accepted until May 16, 2024.

This subsidy is administered in accordance with the university’s “Guidelines for Encouraging Students to Pursue Short-term Study Abroad” and its Implementation Rules.

Eligibility: Graduate and undergraduate students officially enrolled at this university. Priority is given to applicants who hold Republic of China (Taiwan) nationality and have household registration in Taiwan.

Application Period (System Open): From 9:00 AM on April 17, 2024 to 5:00 PM on May 16, 2024.

For required documents and other related information, please refer to the attachment or the Chinese and English webpages of the Office of International Affairs, or contact the project coordinator Ms. Wan-Ching Li at extension 62056.
